f84896e27077de14: KUALA LUMPUR: Taobao is expanding its Malaysia push with AI-powered shopping tools, better local return services and a stronger focus on product quality as it seeks to attract consumers looking beyond low prices for distinctive finds.
The Chinese e-commerce platform is combining AI-driven product discovery with human curation and more local services to make cross-border shopping more convenient for Malaysian consumers.

Taobao Malaysia country head Jess Lew said the company was responding to changing consumer preferences, with shoppers increasingly seeking products that reflect their interests, lifestyles and aspirations.
"Our goal is not only to bring Malaysians access to Everything and Anything, but also to make the experience of discovering and purchasing these products as seamless as possible," she said.
Taobao said Malaysia remained a strategically important market, supported by growing digital commerce activity and demand for products that may be difficult to find locally.

According to the Statistics Department, online retail trade growth for Malaysia accelerated to nine per cent year-on-year in June, alongside research indicating that consumers were increasingly willing to pay more for better-quality products and services.

Taobao said its cross-border catalogue contained more than three billion products, while its new Taobao Curated Supply System had identified more than 4,000 original-brand stores and six million curated products.
The system combines AI and human expertise to assess products based on quality, distinctiveness, price competitiveness and service, helping consumers discover items beyond their usual searches.
AI, LOCALISATION TO DRIVE SHOPPING UPGRADES
A key part of Taobao's strategy is the integration of AI tools to simplify product discovery and help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions.
Taobao Malaysia is introducing four shopping features: AI Try-On, AI Shopping Assistant, AI Product Insights and Voice-Search-by-Hold.

The tools allow users to visualise fashion items on their own photos, receive personalised recommendations, compare product information and summarise customer reviews, or search for items by describing what they need.

The company also said it was strengthening product screening by checking merchants' legal compliance, incorporating consumer feedback and using AI to assess product information including sourcing, quality and copyright.
Products that receive poor consumer feedback may be given lower priority in recommendations.
Lew said Taobao had invested in localising the shopping experience through language support, payment partnerships, logistics improvements and customer service.
These efforts include English and Bahasa Malaysia interfaces, aimed at making the platform more accessible to local consumers.
The latest upgrades are being promoted through Taobao Malaysia's 11.11 Global Shopping Festival, which runs from Oct 20 at 8pm to Nov 13.
The campaign offers free shipping on fashion items without a minimum spending requirement, alongside platform discounts, selected bank rebates and shipping incentives.

The company is also expanding its local after-sales support through a partnership with J&T Express, which will progressively introduce more than 1,400 local return drop-off points nationwide from November.
The network is intended to allow consumers to return eligible purchases locally without having to ship items back to China, addressing a common concern associated with cross-border online shopping.
Taobao Official Logistics also offers parcel tracking, support for delivery issues and compensation for eligible lost or damaged shipments, although the availability of individual services may vary.
The company said the expansion would complement its existing logistics services and give consumers greater confidence when shopping across borders.
MORE MALAYSIAN BRANDS IN CHINA
Beyond bringing Chinese products to Malaysia, Taobao's wider Alibaba ecosystem is exploring opportunities to help Malaysian brands reach consumers in China through Tmall Global.
The company said it had previously supported Malaysian products, including Old Town White Coffee, notable bird's nest brands as well as durian products and footwear, in entering the Chinese market.
It is now exploring ways to bring more Malaysian brands onto Tmall Global in the near future.
The potential expansion could provide local businesses with another route to reach Chinese consumers, alongside Taobao's efforts to widen product access for Malaysian shoppers.
BUILDING CONSUMER CONFIDENCE
Beyond product discovery and promotions, Taobao's expansion of local services highlights the importance of consumer confidence in cross-border e-commerce.
While access to a wider range of products may attract shoppers, delivery costs, return procedures and concerns over product quality can influence whether they make repeat purchases.

Taobao said eligible orders in key Malaysian cities could be upgraded to air shipping, with delivery in as fast as five days. The company is also offering shipping vouchers and other incentives during the campaign.
Its focus on original-brand stores and curated products is intended to help consumers identify distinctive goods, while AI tools aim to simplify comparisons across an extensive selection.
However, the effectiveness of these initiatives will depend on how consistently the platform delivers on its promises, particularly in logistics and after-sales support.

Localising the platform for Malaysia's multicultural market remains a challenge, particularly as products and marketing strategies that resonate with Chinese consumers may not have the same appeal among Malaysian shoppers.
Taobao said it has been experimenting with different campaigns, translations and content creator partnerships to better communicate its products and services to local audiences.
The challenge lies in adapting the shopping experience across different languages, cultural preferences and consumer expectations, while ensuring that product information is clear and relevant.
Building trust in product quality and ensuring reliable cross-border delivery will also be crucial in encouraging first-time users to make repeat purchases.

e5a5302e3b23f81a: GEORGE TOWN: All educational institutions in Penang will operate as usual tomorrow despite the prevailing haze, the Penang Education Department said.
In a statement, the department said it was concerned about the safety and health of students amid the haze affecting the country.
It said students attending school were encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution and drink sufficient water.
"Schools have also been instructed to ensure an adequate supply of drinking water for students and staff," it said.
The department also said parents or guardians concerned about their children's health due to the haze could consider keeping them at home, provided they informed the school administration.
"We will continue to monitor air quality and ensure the safety, health and well-being of students and the education community remain a priority," it added.
bdb15484f1c4a984: KUALA LUMPUR: Buying a new home does not always mean leaving construction defects behind, with recurring waterproofing problems potentially costing homeowners thousands of ringgit after the developer's Defect Liability Period (DLP) expires.

A survey by the National House Buyers Association (HBA) and Nippon Paint Malaysia found that nearly nine in 10 homeowners whose DLP had ended reported waterproofing problems afterwards, raising concerns over the long-term quality of homes and the financial burden of rectifying defects.
Among affected homeowners, 42.4 per cent spent at least RM5,001 on waterproofing repairs, including 14.2 per cent who paid more than RM10,000.

The findings highlight how defects that emerge or recur after the DLP can leave homeowners facing repeated repair costs, disruption and uncertainty over whether the underlying problem has been properly resolved.
HBA honorary secretary-general Datuk Chang Kim Loong said the expiry of the DLP should not mean homeowners stop paying attention to the condition of their properties.
"When waterproofing problems recur or only become apparent later, homeowners can find themselves dealing with repeated repairs, disruption and high out-of-pocket costs," he said.

Chang said homeowners should identify and document defects early, ensure that repair work addresses the actual cause and seek clearer information about the waterproofing systems installed in their properties.

The survey found that 78.2 per cent of affected homeowners required at least two repair attempts or said their problems remained unresolved. Another 61.1 per cent reported recurring issues or were unsure whether the initial repair had fully addressed the problem.

The timing of the defects is also significant. Some 76.3 per cent of homeowners who experienced waterproofing problems after their DLP said the issues emerged either immediately or within the first 12 months after the period ended.
Of these, 12.3 per cent encountered problems immediately after the DLP, 37.7 per cent within six months and 26.3 per cent within a year.
The findings suggest that the end of the formal defect rectification period does not necessarily mark the end of a homeowner's exposure to construction-related problems.

Moreover, many respondents had already encountered waterproofing defects while their homes were still under the DLP. About 88.9 per cent reported waterproofing-related defects during the period, while 76.9 per cent had submitted at least one related defect report.
External walls, bathrooms, and balconies or terraces accounted for 77 per cent of the main areas affected by post-DLP waterproofing problems.
The symptoms extended beyond visible water leaks to include mould and mildew, damp walls, peeling or bubbling paint, ceiling stains and cracks.
Nippon Paint Malaysia general manager Tay Sze Tuck said waterproofing should be viewed as a long-term property protection issue rather than a problem to address only when visible damage appears.

"Once homeowners start spending thousands of ringgit on waterproofing repairs, having to repeat that process becomes more than an inconvenience. The cost can accumulate very quickly when the underlying cause has not been properly identified, and the same problem continues to return," he said.

The financial consequences can extend beyond the immediate repair. Some 74.4 per cent of affected homeowners said waterproofing problems had led to further issues, including mould or hygiene concerns, interior damage, electrical risks and structural damage.
Tay said the source of a leak was not always where the damage appeared, making accurate diagnosis essential before repair work began.

"A stain on a ceiling, peeling paint or mould on a wall may be the visible symptom, but homeowners need to understand what is happening behind it. Getting the diagnosis right is important because every unsuccessful repair can mean another round of cost, disruption and damage," he said.
The survey also exposed gaps in homeowners' knowledge of how serious defects might be and how best to address them.

Half of those affected said assessing the severity of the problem or identifying its root cause was their biggest challenge. Others struggled to determine whom to trust, whether repairs would last, which method to choose and whether the quoted costs were reasonable.

This uncertainty may be contributing to delays in addressing defects. About 80.4 per cent of affected homeowners did not act immediately after noticing signs of waterproofing trouble, instead monitoring the problem, waiting for it to worsen or taking action only when damage became visible indoors.

Access to information about the original waterproofing system was another concern. While 78.7 per cent said knowing the brand or system used in their homes was important to some degree, 66.5 per cent said they had either not been informed or could not remember which brand or system had been installed.

The findings underline the importance of inspecting new homes carefully, reporting defects within the DLP and keeping records of complaints and rectification work. Homeowners should also seek a proper assessment when problems recur rather than repeatedly paying for surface-level repairs.

For buyers, the cost of a new home may therefore extend beyond the purchase price and monthly loan repayments. Persistent defects can create an additional financial burden long after the keys have been handed over.

fd1820e7d2dea277: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The lawsuit filed by professional men’s singles shuttler Lee Zii Jia against his company, LZJ Management Sdn Bhd, and his family was resolved amicably at the High Court here today.
Zii Jia, 28, filed the originating summons against LZJ Management, his father Lee Chee Hin, 59, his sister Zii Yii, 30, and his younger brother Tao, 25, over the company’s management and finances.
Zii Jia’s counsel Ahmad Zayd Ahmad Zuber informed Judge Leong Wai Hong that the parties had reached a settlement and applied for the court to record a consent judgment on the agreed terms.

Reading from the draft consent, Ahmad Zayd said the parties had agreed that an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) of the first respondent (LZJ Management) would be held on October 31, in accordance with the Notice of Extraordinary General Meeting dated October 16, with the costs to be borne by the first respondent.

“Pending the disposal of the EGM, the second and third respondents (Chee Hin and Zii Yii), whether personally, through agents or through any party acting on their behalf, are restrained from approving, paying, disbursing or causing the payment of director’s fees, allowances, bonuses, remuneration or financial benefits (save for monthly salaries, calculated with effect from September 1) to themselves from the first respondent,” he said.

Ahmad Zayd said the second and third respondents are restrained from approving, signing or ratifying any board of directors’ resolution or company resolution, without the court’s leave, save that no order was made as to costs.

Specifically, this covers any resolution relating to the appointment or removal of directors, the appointment of a company secretary, the disposal of material assets, the issuance of new shares, any change in shareholding structure, or any decision affecting the management, administration or control of the first respondent.
After counsel read out the draft consent, Judge Leong asked Zii Jia to come forward to confirm the terms of the settlement.
“Although he is well known, we still need to check his MyKad and verify whether he is the same person,” said the judge, drawing laughter from the media and members of the public present in court.
Judge Leong: Do you agree to the terms of the settlement?

The judge then called Chee Hin and Tao to confirm the terms of the settlement, and both respondents stated that they agreed to the terms. Their counsel, Andrian Ng Chen Yip, informed the court that his other client, Zii Yii, was abroad and had also agreed to the order.
“Thank you to the parties for resolving this case amicably. This is good for all parties, and everyone can move on with their lives,” said Judge Leong.
In today’s proceedings, counsel Samantha Cheng appeared for LZJ Management.

In the originating summons filed on July 2, Zii Jia, who is the majority shareholder of LZJ Management, said he had taken steps to convene an EGM to discuss the management and governance of the company, but had not succeeded in doing so.
Zii Jia holds a 90 per cent stake in the company, while Zii Yii holds nine per cent and Tao one per cent.

The applicant therefore sought an order that the EGM be held within 14 days of the date of the court order and that the meeting proceed notwithstanding the absence of, or refusal to attend by, any member, director or company secretary. — Bernama

f51e39646bdf7750: KUALA LUMPUR: Interpol has issued a Red Notice against Serba Dinamik Holdings Bhd founder Datuk Mohd Abdul Karim Abdullah, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Speaking during Prime Minister's Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) resumed investigating Serba Dinamik transactions in 2023 following further disclosures after charges against the company were withdrawn in May 2022.
The probe also extended to related cases, including Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd (SCIB), which involves Karim.
On March 12 this year, the SC said it had obtained a warrant of arrest against Karim, 61, a former SCIB chairman and non-executive, non-independent director who was then at large.

The regulator said the public prosecutor had consented to prosecuting Karim for allegedly causing SCIB to furnish a false statement to Bursa Malaysia. He was wanted for an offence under Section 369(b)(B) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007.

Karim was previously charged in 2021 over false information in Serba Dinamik's financial statements. The case was later resolved through a RM3 million compound after the public prosecutor accepted his representation.
Anwar said the SC had initiated 239 criminal charges against 50 individuals as part of stepped-up enforcement against corporate crime.
He said the enforcement efforts included cases that had been at risk of being closed in May 2022, when the SC withdrew all charges against Serba Dinamik.

"Following continued disclosures about the matter, the SC began investigating transactions involving not only Serba Dinamik from 2023 onwards, but also related cases, including Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd, which involves Datuk Karim. Most recently, Interpol issued a Red Notice against him.
"This demonstrates an increase in the Securities Commission's enforcement actions, both criminal and civil," he said.
81f1edc66d746e11: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has yet to decide which logo its candidates will use in the Melaka election.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition had sufficient time to finalise its decision on the seats to contest, candidates to field and logo to use.
He said the matter would be discussed with component parties Pas, Gerakan, Parti Wawasan Negara and Pejuang before a decision could be made.
"This is nothing unusual. We have yet to make a decision as there is still plenty of time. We will decide which seats to contest, the candidates to field and the logo to use.
"The 31st (Oct 31, nomination day for the Melaka election) is not two days away. We still have plenty of time," he told a press conference at Parliament today.
Takiyuddin said the use of a common logo was not new in Malaysian politics, citing the 2018 14th General Election, when Pakatan Harapan (PH) component parties used the PKR logo.
He said PN had 62 MPs supporting the coalition in Parliament.
"We have 62 MPs who stand together in support of PN. We have a shared responsibility towards the people," he said.

In a related development, Takiyuddin said PN's court application, scheduled to be heard on Thursday, also sought to protect Melaka voters' right to choose their representatives in the Nov 14 state election.
He said the legal action was not solely to protect PN's interests, but also to defend the rights of the people of Melaka, particularly the more than 600,000 eligible voters.
He claimed voters would be denied the opportunity to vote for PN if the coalition were barred from contesting the election.
"This is not just about PN's interests, but also those of the people, particularly the people of Melaka," he said.

Earlier, the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) confirmed it had cancelled PN's registration, saying the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
RoS said the decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after reviewing documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
It said an earlier notice dated Sept 22 had been issued under subsection 13(2) of the Act, giving the coalition 30 days to explain why its registration should not be cancelled.

89cbb9e19dc06d5c: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to disclose the extent of public funds exposed to the collapse in Zetrix AI Bhd's share price.
Rafizi described Zetrix, formerly MyEG Services Bhd, as a company of significant public interest, with activities that have major implications for national security.
He said the company's closing share price fell from 75.5 sen on April 1 to five sen on Oct 19, a decline of 93.4 per cent in six months. The sell-off began on Aug 28.
"No member of parliament or political party has yet focused on the implications of Zetrix's share price collapse," he said in a statement.

Based on publicly available financial reports, Rafizi said three public funds held shares in Zetrix. The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) held 67,674,000 shares and Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) held 211,507,500 shares as at April 1, while Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP) held 390,090,000 shares as at Oct 2, 2025.
The funds' latest holdings are unknown and will not be reported until Zetrix's 2026 annual report is finalised, he said.
Assuming the funds still held the shares when the sell-off began, Rafizi said they faced potential losses of RM472 million, based on a decline of 70.5 sen per share.

Rafizi also raised concerns about the National Integrated Immigration System (NIISe), a RM1.05 billion contract awarded to HeiTech Padu Bhd in 2024. HeiTech Padu had named Zetrix as its technology partner.

He said that when HeiTech Padu won the contract in 2024, its two largest shareholders were Rosetta Partners Sdn Bhd, jointly controlled by the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V, and Farhash Wafa Salvador, and Zetrix.
Rafizi said Zetrix sold its entire 16.9 per cent stake in HeiTech Padu on Sept 2 amid its financial crisis, raising questions about its role as a technology provider for NIISe.
He called on Anwar to disclose how many Zetrix shares government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies, including Maybank and CIMB, held on April 1.

He also asked the prime minister to disclose how many Zetrix shares the funds still held as at Oct 20, and how much they had lost on shares already sold and how much their remaining shares had fallen in value.
He also sought clarification on which company was now providing the technology for NIISe.
50c3ed7000be41af: TOKYO: Tokyo residents opposed to a planned logistics and data centre complex announced the creation of a lawsuit group on Tuesday and expect to file a civil case this year against GLP Japan to halt the project.
The lawsuit is Japan's first civil lawsuit against a data centre operator
The planned 3.63-million-megawatt data centre development in Akishima, western Tokyo includes three logistics buildings and eight data centre buildings
Residents are concerned the data centre would threaten wildlife, drain their water supply, generate pollution and cause a spike in electricity usage
The planned lawsuit follows years of campaigning that residents say has not changed GLP's plans
It underscores the growing friction between Japan's push to expand digital infrastructure and local residents concerned about the environmental and social impact of data centre development
71fe33bf979b744b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) plans to streamline and consolidate more than 300 registered Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans’ associations to facilitate the distribution of assistance to the group, said its Deputy Minister Adly Zahari.

He said under the initiative, to be implemented by the National Veterans Council and the Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV), the number of associations would be reduced to 100, with the associations operating under parent associations to enable government assistance schemes to be coordinated more effectively.
“At the same time, the ministry is also considering increasing the contributions or allocations that we have provided.

“We also hope the state governments will continue to support and encourage veterans’ associations, as JHEV’s focus is on ensuring the welfare of veterans,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a supplementary question from Commander (Rtd) Nordin Ahmad Ismail (PN-Lumut), who wanted to know what steps the ministry or JHEV was taking to coordinate the registration of veterans’ associations with state governments.

In response to a supplementary question from RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) on the possibility of re-employing veterans at the country’s main entry points, Adly said the government had begun recruiting veterans into the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) this year.
“When AKPS recruits veterans, we can shorten the training process by up to six months because they already have expertise in national defence.
“Similarly, air force veterans with technical expertise can be readily absorbed into the defence industry,” he said.
Adly said the ministry had also allocated funds under Budget 2026 and Budget 2027 to enable former military personnel to be recruited as forest rangers.
He said the move would not only help reduce government expenditure but also make use of veterans’ expertise in the security sector and safeguard national sovereignty. — Bernama
97191be0e6be73e4: KUALA LUMPUR: The Retirement Fund Inc's (KWAP) recent investment in Jakarta exposed major weaknesses in its process due to excessive reliance on international trends and external institutions, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the incident underscored the need for stricter safeguards and greater accountability in managing public funds, despite the fund's existing due diligence and investment committee procedures.
"In this case, we relied on SoftBank, assuming it would not make a careless investment, but that turned out to be the case.

"I acknowledge the shortcomings. However, we cannot deny KWAP's overall achievements in recording substantial profits. That is clear, but we must also acknowledge the weaknesses," he said during Prime Minister's Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Anwar was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran), who asked about substantial losses suffered by KWAP, measures to identify those responsible, and steps to tighten investment procedures to prevent future losses.

He said the fund's existing due diligence and investment committee procedures were structured and stringent, but the investment exposed a critical flaw in relying on international trends and external institutional judgment, including major European and Japanese firms.
He said the government will further tighten regulations and procedures to ensure public funds entrusted to KWAP are managed responsibly.
671d7a8920bd9cf7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — A joint study by Lazada and Cube Asia has highlighted a US$900 million (approximately RM3.67 billion) annual e-commerce spending gap in Malaysia, driven by distinct differences in how consumers approach online shopping.

The findings, presented today by Cube Asia co-founder Simon Torring, reveal that while only one in five Malaysian online shoppers qualifies as a “savvy shopper”, this group spends 36 per cent more each month than the average consumer.

The report, titled 2026 eCommerce Savvy Shopper Report: Southeast Asia, defines “savvy shoppers” as those who meet specific benchmarks across four dimensions: verification of product details, value optimisation, confidence and protection, and digital fluency.
Torring noted that Malaysia’s current share of savvy shoppers stands at 20 per cent, slightly below the 24 per cent regional average.
“While Malaysia’s savvy shopper share is below the 24 per cent regional average, the research points to an opportunity to strengthen shopping habits, particularly in verification,” Torring said.
The study indicates that 17 per cent of local consumers are classified as “near-savvy,” meeting three out of the four benchmarks.
Notably, 45 per cent of this group identify verification — the act of checking product details, reviews, and authenticity — as the only barrier preventing them from reaching full “savvy” status.
The report highlighted that price is no longer the sole determinant of value for the Malaysian consumer.
Instead, factors such as product authenticity, seller credibility, and robust purchase protection play significant roles in purchasing decisions.
According to the data, 39 per cent of savvy shoppers are willing to pay more for better purchase protection, compared to just 24 per cent of general shoppers.
Furthermore, 43 per cent of savvy shoppers direct the majority of their spending to “Mall” sections of marketplaces, reflecting a higher preference for trusted environments.

Lazada Malaysia chief executive officer Kaya Qin said the findings highlight the platform’s commitment to empowering consumers to make more informed decisions, particularly as household budgets remain a top priority.
“Our aim is to help Malaysians spend well, rather than spend more,” Qin said.
“Whether it is groceries for the week, school supplies, or a new appliance, making every ringgit count matters at every income level. A good deal should not end at the checkout,” she said.
Qin added that shoppers should be able to compare the full cost, know who they are buying from, and have confidence in the support available after purchase.
“The company is prioritising initiatives to make trusted sellers more identifiable and protection more accessible to help bridge the gap.

“For Lazada, this means making trusted sellers easier to identify, offers easier to compare, and protection more accessible. It is also how brands and sellers can earn consumer confidence, build credibility and encourage repeat business,” she said.

The research suggests that as more consumers adopt these habits, platforms, brands, and sellers will be incentivised to improve transparency and service, potentially elevating the standards of the wider eCommerce ecosystem in Malaysia.

The study, which surveyed 6,000 online shoppers aged 18 to 61 across six Southeast Asian markets, utilised survey-reported differences in monthly spending and weighted market shares to calculate the US$900 million gap.
The US$900 million estimate is based on the spending gap between savvy and general shoppers, adjusted to reflect their actual share of the total market.
The researchers highlighted that the figure tracks the higher purchasing power of savvy shoppers, rather than suggesting that being a savvy shopper itself creates additional, unexpected spending.
40265c1ba09a082d: KUALA LUMPUR: Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah received another timely boost after climbing back into the world's top four in the latest Badminton World Federation (BWF) rankings released today.
Fresh from ending Malaysia's 18-year wait for a women's doubles title at the Denmark Open on Sunday, the pair rose one spot to world No. 4 — their highest position since June.
The improvement is an encouraging sign for Pearly-Thinaah, who were ranked world No. 2 in early June before slipping to fifth, a position they had occupied for more than four months.
Their return to the top four comes after they defeated Japan's Hinata Suzuki-Nao Yamakita 21-18, 21-11 in the Denmark Open final to claim their first title since January.
The improved ranking also strengthens their prospects of securing favourable seedings in upcoming tournaments, with the top four seeds generally kept apart until the semi-finals.
For now, the Malaysians will be keen to build on their renewed momentum at the French Open, which begins today.
Seeded second in Paris, Pearly-Thinaah will be hoping for another memorable campaign at the tournament where they captured their breakthrough Super 750 title in 2022.
Meanwhile, men's doubles aces Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik remained fourth in the world despite reaching the Denmark Open final.

The former world champions finished runners-up to Indonesia's Fajar Alfian-Muhammad Shohibul Fikri, but their performance in Odense, which included a semi-final victory over world No. 1 Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae of South Korea, was nevertheless an encouraging return following their reunion.

In mixed doubles, rising professional pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing enjoyed one of the biggest gains among Malaysian shuttlers, jumping 20 places to world No. 31 following their Denmark Open semi-final appearance.
Their rise into the world's top 32 also secures them entry into all levels of the World Tour, including the prestigious Super 750 and Super 1000 tournaments.
Men's doubles pair Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin improved one spot to world No. 5 following their quarter-final appearance in Denmark.
Arctic Open champions Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King continued their rapid rise, jumping another 21 places to world No. 95 after reaching the Denmark Open second round.
The promising combination have now climbed an impressive 253 places over the past two ranking updates.

Elsewhere, husband-and-wife pair Goh Soon Huat-Shevon Lai rose one place to ninth in mixed doubles, while Jimmy Wong-Cheng Su Yin moved up nine spots to 41st.Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun improved one place to 11th in men's doubles.
In singles, Leong Jun Hao slipped one rung to world No. 31, while Lee Zii Jia remained 42nd.
Justin Hoh dropped one spot to 46th.K. Letshanaa retained her position at world No. 27 in women's singles, while Wong Ling Ching fell three places to 40th.
f0e20aa75e07f676: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Candidates sitting the Certificate in Legal Practice (CLP) examination are assessed purely on merit, with no quota imposed on the number of passes, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.

Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said candidates were assessed based on their performance, with a minimum passing mark set for each subject.
“The passing mark for each CLP subject is 40, and there is no quota for passes. Candidates are assessed purely on merit,” he said during the question-and-answer session.

He was responding to a supplementary question from Dr V. Sivakumar (PH-Batu Gajah) on measures to address the low CLP examination pass rate while maintaining professional standards, after only 19 per cent of candidates (158 out of 826) obtained a full pass in 2026, compared with 21 per cent in 2025.
Kulasegaran clarified that the statistics covered only the main 2026 CLP examination and did not include the results of the supplementary examination.
“The overall results of the 2026 CLP examination will be announced in November 2026, after the results of the supplementary examination have been obtained and approved by the Board,” he said.

On the factors contributing to candidates’ failure, Kulasegaran said most candidates were law graduates from the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand, where they had studied the common law system, but appeared not to have adequately prepared for the Malaysian law component of the CLP examination.
He said that candidates also had difficulty identifying legal issues in examination questions, applying the law to the facts and citing relevant case law to support their answers.

In response to Sivakumar’s original question on the CLP’s structure, assessment methods, duration of study and transition to the New Bar Course (NBC), Kulasegaran said the Legal Profession Qualifying Board had established an NBC Task Force on April 27.

He said the task force was tasked with conducting a study to develop an implementation framework for the NBC, including arrangements to ensure a smooth transition to the new professional legal qualification system.

Kulasegaran said the NBC, which would replace the CLP, comprises two programmes, namely the Conversion Course (CC) and the Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate (LPPC), with a greater emphasis on practical legal skills and professional competence.

He said the existing CLP system assesses candidates solely through written examinations, without a comprehensive evaluation of their practical legal skills, and does not require them to complete preparatory courses before sitting the examinations.

On the transition from the CLP to the NBC, he explained that the NBC Task Force was reviewing policies concerning candidates who had yet to pass the existing examinations but still had remaining attempts and valid registration periods.
“The qualifying board will consider this matter once the NBC Task Force has completed its study on the transition mechanism,” he said.

Responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut) on checks and balances in setting the curriculum and assessing prospective lawyers, Kulasegaran said the professional legal qualification system would continue under an improved approach with a revised set of courses.

He said that the improvements took into account complaints about the previous system while emphasising the difference between academic legal studies and the professional training required to become a lawyer.

Kulasegaran explained that law programmes in the United Kingdom and several other countries typically take three years to complete, compared with four years at local universities, where a professional component is introduced in the fourth year. — Bernama
e135aec6185885b8: JAKARTA: Indonesian authorities were investigating on Tuesday after a car-sized piece of what a government agency said was a Chinese space rocket crashed into a palm oil plantation near homes and work sites.

The debris was found on Monday morning by a plantation worker in Indonesian Borneo, after residents reported hearing a loud bang the previous evening over a remote area of Central Kalimantan province.
"It was just there. At first, I thought it might have been aircraft debris," Wardi Tamroni told AFP of his discovery near the town of Sampit.
Wardi, 51, said the object had crashed about three kilometres from the housing complex of the PT Agro Bukit palm oil company he works for.
"We usually carry out our activities in the area where the object fell," he added.
"Fortunately, all the workers had already gone home, so no one was left in the plantation."
Local police chief I Kadek Dwi Yoga Sidhimantra described the object as "a fairly large aluminium plate measuring up to nine metres with an irregular shape and visible burn marks."
The incident did not cause loss of life or property damage, according to civil aviation spokesman Zachrudien, who like many Indonesians has one name.
The debris also posed no radiation or toxicity risks, he added.
Indonesia's National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN) said the debris appeared to come from a Chinese Zhuque-2E rocket.
The Chinese government said last week that a Zhuque-2E rocket had launched 10 satellites into space from a commercial launch site in the country's northwest.
BRIN researcher Thomas Djamaluddin said in a statement that not all parts of a spacecraft necessarily burn up on re-entry into Earth's atmosphere, and more heat-resistant parts may reach the surface.
"This phenomenon is one possible explanation for the discovery of a large metal fragment in a palm oil plantation in Sampit," he said.

Debris usually crashes into the oceans which cover about 70 per cent of Earth's surface, and the European Space Agency says casualty risk to individuals on Earth due to uncontrolled re-entry is "extremely low", though growing as launches increase.
The China National Space Administration could not be immediately reached for comment.--AFP
4627e8d62d2dcd64: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke wants Transport Expo Asia (TXA) to become a permanent biennial event, with the next edition set for 2028 to showcase transport technologies and innovation.
He said the exhibition would bring together industry players, promote international best practices and support the development of Malaysia’s transport industry.
“I hope that TXA will be organised once every two years,” he said when opening the expo at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) today.

Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah and Transport Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan.
Held from Oct 20 to 22, TXA 2026 serves as a key meeting point for the land, aviation, maritime and logistics sectors.
Loke said the idea for a dedicated transport exhibition emerged from the ministry’s co-organising of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA).
He said LIMA’s growing popularity and increasingly constrained exhibition space prompted the ministry to consider holding its own event, while allowing LIMA to focus more on the defence industry.
“I brought a proposal to the Cabinet two years ago for the ministry to branch out from LIMA, leading to an inaugural TXA event on a smaller scale last year,” he said.

This year’s exhibition features 410 exhibitors and technology innovators, providing a platform to connect public policy with industry innovation and translate collaboration into improved transport services, stronger trade links and new economic opportunities.

Loke said the technologies on show across the 15,000-square-metre exhibition hall, alongside autonomous vehicle demonstrations and strategic agreements, were expected to bring tangible improvements in efficiency, emissions reduction, safety and reliability.

Speaking to reporters after the opening ceremony, Loke said government spending on transport infrastructure and maintenance should create more opportunities for Malaysian companies across the supply chain.
He said original equipment manufacturers and suppliers could use TXA to connect with local businesses, helping government expenditure support domestic manufacturing and component supply.
“Rail, aviation and road transport require extensive supply chains, creating opportunities for Malaysian companies to supply components and support maintenance activities,” he said.

On the expo’s economic impact, Loke said no target had been set for its first large-scale edition. However, several memoranda of understanding and agreements are expected to be signed during the three-day event.
He encouraged logistics companies and transport-related small and medium enterprises (SMEs)to explore the technologies on display and pursue potential business opportunities. — Bernama
9a35f2fca8bac24f: HANOI: Vietnam's capital Hanoi has launched a large-scale programme to prune hundreds of its iconic blackboard trees and is considering relocating some after their distinctive fragrance proved too much for some residents.

Known in Vietnamese as hoa sua, meaning "milk flower", and also known as pulai and devil's tree elsewhere in Asia, blackboard trees can grow as tall as 60 metres. The name reflects the traditional use of its wood for school items, as does its scientific name, Alstonia scholaris.

Blackboard trees have lined Hanoi's boulevards since they were introduced during French colonial rule in the late 19th century. They were later planted across the capital, and Hanoi now has about 14,400 of the trees, according to the city government.

At dusk, the trees release a pungent, sweet scent from their greenish-white flowers, peaking in September and October. Long associated with the arrival of autumn in Hanoi, they have inspired hit songs and poetry for decades.
But many of the city's nearly 9 million residents say the fragrance is overpowering.
"I simply cannot stand the smell," said Hanoi resident Nguyen Ha Long, 43, who said he stopped his evening runs because the scent gave him migraines.

After years of complaints and smaller interventions, local authorities have launched their largest pruning campaign yet, stripping the flowers from about 7 per cent of Hanoi's blackboard trees during a five-day blitz ending on Tuesday.

Officials also plan to relocate trees from streets where they are most heavily concentrated, adding to the impact of major public works projects underway in Hanoi that are rapidly reshaping the city's landscape as the ruling Communist Party chases ultra-fast economic growth.

"I absolutely love the scent of blackboard trees. The stronger the fragrance, the more I love it," said Nguyen Thu Trang, 37, who lives on central Nguyen Du, a street lined with blackboard trees and which was also the setting of the best-selling novel "The Sorrow of War."
"My family has lived here for over 30 years, and we all love the scent. I feel deeply saddened seeing the city prune them," she added.

"The smell is not toxic," said Tran Cong Khanh, head of Vietnam's ethnomedicine research centre, echoing views expressed by three other Vietnamese scientists interviewed by Reuters, who however recommend limiting concentrations in densely populated areas because the pollen, like that of other plants, can trigger allergic reactions.
The debate has been widely reported by local newspapers, despite public health rarely ranking among Vietnamese residents' top concerns.
By contrast, air pollution, which often makes Hanoi one of the world's most polluted cities during winter, has generally attracted less public attention.--REUTERS
6c633af0476dae0a: KUALA LUMPUR: Express bus operators will not suffer losses under the new requirement for tickets to be sold through terminals licensed by the Land Public Transport Agency (Apad), Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
He said operators had yet to fully understand the policy, adding that the ministry would hold engagement sessions to explain the move.
"There will be an engagement session to explain it to them. There is no loss to the bus companies," he said after opening the Transport Expo Asia 2026.
His remarks followed Apad's announcement that express bus tickets could only be sold through licensed terminals from Nov 1.

Malaysian Bus Operators Association president Datuk Mohamad Ashfar Ali said the change had raised concerns among operators who had invested in developing their own websites and ticketing systems to facilitate ticket purchases.

Loke said the policy was aimed at restricting online ticketing agents (OTAs), which were mostly based overseas, from selling bus tickets and collecting commissions without providing services at the terminals.
"We want to restrict the OTAs. They sell these tickets and receive commissions, but they do not provide any services, including managing any services at the terminal," he said.
He added that the government also faced difficulties regulating OTAs, particularly when passengers sought refunds for services that were not provided.
"They are not licence holders. They sell the tickets, but if the service is not provided, we cannot regulate them when it comes to getting refunds," he said.
He said the move would improve ticket sales and terminal management while ensuring bus operators were not burdened with additional charges.
Loke said the government had ensured terminal operators could not charge more than the existing rates and hoped they would reduce the charges to provide better returns for bus companies.

Asked when engagement with bus operators would take place, Loke said discussions would be conducted between terminal operators and bus companies, as the matter involved business-to-business transactions.
"We only make the policy decision. In terms of transactions, it is between the terminal and the bus operators," he said.
f196206908fb6dda: PETALING JAYA: Pengerusi Perikatan Nasional (PN) Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar menegaskan gelombang sokongan rakyat terhadap gabungan itu tidak akan mudah dipadam susulan pembatalan pendaftarannya oleh Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM).
Dalam hantaran di Facebook, Samsuri mempersoalkan masa keputusan berkenaan dibuat ketika pertikaian berkaitan tindakan JPPM terhadap PN masih dalam proses mahkamah.
“Apa yang berlaku sehari sebelum kes dibawa ke mahkamah adalah satu tindakan luar biasa. Memang luar biasa, yang boleh jadi luar tabii,” katanya.
Beliau turut mendakwa beberapa tindakan terhadap PN menjelang PRN Melaka menunjukkan wujud motif politik dan “ketakutan” terhadap gabungan itu.
Menurutnya, Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya (SPR) juga baru-baru ini meminta PN memberikan maklum balas berhubung penggunaan logo gabungan itu pada pilihan raya berkenaan.

“Semua tindakan yang selari dengan garis masa sebelum pengisytiharan calon pilihan raya Melaka, dalam keadaan pihak SPR baru dua hari lalu menghantar surat kepada PN untuk memberi respons penggunaan logo PN, adalah jelas bermotifkan ketakutan kepada gabungan ini.
"Ingatlah, gelombang rakyat tidak akan mudah padam dengan tindakan orang politik yang berselindung di sebalik kuasa," kata menteri besar Terengganu itu.
Awal hari ini, JPPM membatalkan pendaftaran PN selepas mendapati penjelasan dikemukakan gabungan itu gagal menyangkal asas pembatalan yang dinyatakan dalam notis terdahulu.
Keputusan itu dibuat mengikut subperenggan 13(1)(c)(iv) Akta Pertubuhan 1966 selepas JPPM meneliti keseluruhan dokumen dan representasi dikemukakan PN pada 12 Okt.
PN sebelum ini memfailkan permohonan semakan kehakiman bagi mencabar tindakan JPPM, manakala permohonan berkaitan penangguhan tindakan terhadap gabungan itu dijadual didengar pada 22 Okt.

Setiausaha Agung PN Takiyuddin Hassan turut berkata gabungan itu akan mencabar pembatalan pendaftarannya dan memohon supaya pelaksanaan serta kesannya ditangguhkan sementara menunggu keputusan mahkamah.
PRN Melaka ditetapkan pada 14 Nov, dengan penamaan calon pada 31 Okt dan pengundian awal pada 10 Nov.
51ac21e29f96890f: The party must aspire to be more than a Labour pressure group. It should offer a vision for radical reform – and ways to implement it It’s a strange time to be a Green. We have just held our largest conference ever, but it was overshadowed by a controversial motion that was attacked by the media as racist. 9d01551da782fa1a: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is in talks with Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia to establish a land transit route for fresh durian exports to China, potentially lowering transport costs and making Malaysian durians more affordable.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said negotiations and consultations with the four countries were progressing smoothly.
He said the ministry was working with the Foreign and Transport ministries to facilitate the talks.

"Land transportation is expected to take only three to four days, allowing durians to be delivered quickly and marketed in China," he said in reply to a supplementary question from Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng).
Tan had asked about the progress of negotiations with the four countries to improve cross-border transport efficiency for exports, particularly durians, to China.
Mohamad said Malaysian durians were popular among Chinese consumers, but high air freight costs made the fruit more expensive in China.
He said the proposed route would involve transit arrangements through the four Asean countries, adding that negotiations could be challenging as they also exported durians to China.
"Nonetheless, we are continuing negotiations, as our market share in China is not as large as theirs," he said.
Mohamad said Malaysia initiated negotiations on July 20 to secure transit arrangements for shipments passing through the four countries before reaching China.
The government was also exploring the possibility of exporting durians by sea, although the journey would take considerably longer.
"Many durian enthusiasts in China want fresh durians. Therefore, fresh durians could be transported either by air or by rail," he said.

In response to the original question, Mohamad said 97 memorandums of understanding worth RM10.35 billion were secured during the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agro-Tourism Exhibition 2026. These included deals worth RM3.27 billion with strategic partners from China.
He said the agreements were expected to boost production and processing capacity, facilitate technology transfer and strengthen the agri-food sector's value chain.

"To ensure the MoU commitments translate into actual implementation, the ministry will undertake follow-up action with relevant agencies and industry players by facilitating investment-related issues, coordinating stakeholders and monitoring project progress through to the implementation stage," he said.
890f94f2430ae69c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysia and the World Health Organization (WHO) have renewed their joint commitment to finalise the landmark WHO Pandemic Agreement by May 2027, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said Malaysia is emphasising the need to strike a balance between intellectual property rights protection and equitable access to medical countermeasures during health emergencies.

Dzulkefly said this was among the key issues he discussed with WHO director-general Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus during a courtesy call on the sidelines of the 77th session of the WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific (WPRO), held in Manila, from Oct 19 to 22.

“WHO also expressed strong confidence in Malaysia by inviting the country to play a strategic leadership role in the Western Pacific region, working alongside regional countries to build global consensus on emergency preparedness,” he said in a Facebook post today.
During the meeting, he said Malaysia also reiterated its firm commitment to supporting sustainable financing for WHO.

“Meanwhile, Dr Tedros’ appreciation of the progress made in Malaysia’s ongoing primary healthcare (PHC) transformation efforts was a great source of encouragement for Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel,” he added. — Bernama
c48a8787ef85f041: PETALING JAYA: The government inherited a system that lacks transparency, allowing corporate crimes and market manipulation to go largely unchecked for decades, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said today.

He said weaknesses in the previous system meant enforcement action was rarely taken in major cases involving billions of ringgit in losses, including corporate takeovers and banking transactions allegedly influenced by political interference.

Anwar alleged that several cases involving so-called corporate mafia activities were linked to a former finance minister whom he said wielded considerable influence and controlled substantial financial resources.

"We inherited a system that lacked transparency. MPs who have followed developments since the 1980s and 1990s would know how major companies, such as Multi-Purpose Holdings Bhd, were allegedly forced to be sold to a group led by Akbar Khan.

"All this was linked to the former finance minister at the time, who had considerable influence and financial resources," he was quoted as saying by Bernama in response to Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) in the Dewan Rakyat.
Aminuddin had sought an update on alleged corporate mafia activities and the enforcement actions taken so far.

Anwar cited several other cases which he said underscored the need for enforcement agencies, including Bank Negara Malaysia, the Securities Commission (SC) Malaysia, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and the police, to carry out their duties in a transparent manner.

"RHB Bank was successfully managed by Rashid Hussain, but he was forced to relinquish his stake and eventually lost control. Those who subsequently held ownership were also linked to the former finance minister.
"Phileo Allied Bank was among the fastest growing banks at the time, but the former finance minister directed banks to consolidate.
"It was subsequently relinquished because of the former minister's interests in Langkah Bahagia Sdn Bhd, which later acquired a stake in the company," he said.
Anwar also said the SC had increased enforcement action in corporate crime cases by two to three times since 2023 compared with previous years.
8fafac3ef50950e5: KUANTAN: Police dismantled an online scam call centre syndicate following five raids across Kuantan and Genting Highlands, Bentong between Oct 6 and Oct 14.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said 31 people, comprising four locals and 27 foreigners, were arrested for alleged involvement in the syndicate.
He said the arrested foreigners included 25 Chinese citizens, one Indian citizen, and one Myanmar citizen.
"During the operation, police seized various equipment, including computers, laptops, mobile phones, and cash amounting to RM4,850.

"The case is being investigated under Section 420 and Section 120B of the Penal Code, as well as relevant provisions under the Immigration Act," he said at a press conference at the Pahang Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
Azry Akmar said initial investigations revealed the operations were conducted in an organised manner with specific task delegations.
He added that the syndicate utilised fake social media accounts, messaging applications, and internet networks to deceive victims and conceal their true identities.
"The syndicate's modus operandi included online investment scams, love scams, and part-time job offer scams targeting victims from China, Europe, and the United States," he said.
8a290555e0f24944: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — A total of 124 Universiti Malaya (UM) researchers, including vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Seri Noor Azuan Abu Osman, have been named among the world’s top 2 per cent of scientists in the latest Stanford University–Elsevier global ranking.

The ranking, based on the single-year 2026 dataset, uses standardised citation-based indicators to identify influential scientists worldwide. It measures the impact of their published research within the international scientific community.
Noor Azuan, who is among those recognised, said the achievement showed that Malaysian scholarship could hold its own internationally.
“With 124 of our researchers recognised among the world’s leading scientists, Universiti Malaya is demonstrating that Malaysian scholarship can compete, lead and shape global scientific discourse.
“We are not content to follow the world’s intellectual frontiers. We aspire to redefine them,” he said in a statement.
He said international recognition came with a greater responsibility to ensure scientific advancement delivered meaningful and lasting impact.
“Our ambition is unequivocal: to transform research excellence into global influence, scientific discovery into human progress, and Malaysian talent into enduring global leadership.
“This recognition reflects not only the intellectual strength of our researchers, but also our collective responsibility to ensure that knowledge creates lasting impact,” he added.

UM said the recognition reflected its commitment to building world-class research talent and interdisciplinary collaboration. It said the achievement carried particular significance as the university marks its 121st anniversary this year.

The university said it would continue to nurture research talent, build partnerships with leading global institutions and industries, and turn its research into contributions to economic development, technological advancement and societal well-being.
edc820e0eeb212e0: CALGARY: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the US.

CBC News, Canada's government-funded national broadcaster, called the result late Monday after 33% of the vote had been counted. At the time of the call, 76% of tallied votes were in support of the "remain" side versus 23% in favor of the province moving forward with a binding vote on separation. The referendum was nonbinding.
"Albertans made a clear choice," Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement. "They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other."
"Canada is greater than the sum of its parts," he said.

Pollsters and analysts had repeatedly dismissed the possibility of a separatist victory, citing data that showed about one-third of residents in the western province supported a future referendum on leaving.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced the referendum in May, saying it was “time to have a vote, understand the will of Albertans on this subject, and move on.”

Late Monday, Smith issued a statement on social media saying she was "very pleased" that early results show widespread support for remaining in Canada. She said she would address Albertans on Tuesday to discuss the results and "where our province goes from here."

A small but vocal group of separatists has campaigned for months for an independent Alberta, arguing that the province’s energy wealth is subsidizing poorer parts of Canada and that Alberta would be far richer without Ottawa bureaucracy impeding its path.

Last week, Carney told a rally in Calgary that voting to leave Canada would be “a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep division,” and appealed to Albertans to “vote like Canada depends on it.”

Carney, who grew up mostly in Alberta, acknowledged that Albertans have often felt slighted by Ottawa and said his government had approved a proposed new pipeline, adding that Alberta is critical to helping Canada reduce its dependence on the US.
Alberta's referendum follows two previous referendums on separation in the majority French-speaking province of Quebec. Quebecers voted to stay in Canada in both instances.
First Nations groups have also objected to the idea of an independent Alberta, as their land treaties with Ottawa predate the province’s creation within Canada.

CBC News reported strong turnout from First Nations. One southern Alberta polling station in an area that is home to the Siksika Nation temporarily ran out of ballots, and then stayed open until after 10 p.m. MT (0400 GMT) to ensure everyone in line had the chance to vote.

Still, Monday’s referendum is unlikely to end the separatist movement in Alberta. Before the referendum, some separatist leaders said they would continue to pursue another vote even if most Albertans voted to remain.
According to data released on Oct 16 by the pollster Angus Reid, 62% of Albertans believe “there will never be an end to the separatist movement” in the province.

Alberta's referendum also included nine other nonbinding questions on topics including immigration, access to provincial services — such as education, social care and healthcare — and voter identification requirements. Results for those questions were still trickling in.
0c74136bf5bffb18: KOTA BARU: A man arrested for allegedly committing an indecent act against a cat in Pasir Puteh has three previous criminal offences involving drugs and housebreaking.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the 49-year-old suspect has been remanded.
He said the cat has been sent to the Veterinary Services Department to assess its injuries.
"Investigations revealed that the suspect kept 11 cats. The remaining 10 cats were taken by the police alongside a non-governmental organisation (NGO) last night.
"The suspect is unmarried and has three criminal offences, including drug offences and housebreaking.
"However, his urine test upon arrest returned negative," he said at a press conference after the Kelantan police headquarters monthly assembly here today.
The man was arrested yesterday assist investigations into a viral social media video allegedly showing an indecent act involving a cat.
Pasir Puteh police chief Superintendent Saari Yaacob had said that the arrest followed a police report lodged on Sunday.
"The case is being investigated under Section 377 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act," he said in a statement.
003a6765a58f760b: PETALING JAYA: The Islamic development department (Jakim) has launched an investigation following videos on social media platform Threads of chickens allegedly being processed in unhygienic and potentially non-halal conditions.

"A thorough investigation is being conducted with local authorities regarding the company, which is not a Malaysian halal certificate holder, related to the issue which has gone viral," it said in a statement on its social media accounts.
Putrajaya MP Radzi Jidin was among those who raised concerns about the videos, calling for an investigation into issues including the method of slaughter and halal status of the chickens.
He also submitted a formal complaint to Jakim and notified the office of the religious affairs minister.
"The issue of halal (status) and food safety should not be taken lightly," he was reported as saying by Astro Awani.
6266acdca15e0c58: PASIR PUTEH: A cutting board maker has been remanded for seven days to assist investigations into an indecent act involving a cat in Selinsing here.
The remand order, effective today until next Monday, was issued by magistrate Nik Mohd Fadli Datuk Nik Azlan.
The 49-year-old suspect was arrested at 10am yesterday following a police report over the circulation of a 56-second video.
The suspect arrived at court at 9am, handcuffed and escorted by police. He was wearing a black T-shirt and cream-coloured trousers.
The unmarried suspect has previous criminal offences for drugs and housebreaking.
The case is being investigated under Section 377 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
The video sparked outrage among animal lovers and members of the public, who called for legal action against the suspect.
Police are also investigating claims that the suspect has mental health issues.
b39f72c706d88580: GEORGE TOWN: Penang will intensify efforts to tackle pollution in Sungai Kereh, insisting that its causes must be established through evidence before action is taken against offenders.

State Local Government Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the state government was taking the long-running pollution issue seriously, following calls by Tasek Gelugor member of parliament Datuk Wan Saiful Wan Jan to halt pig farming in the constituency and consider a nationwide ban.
Kampung Selamat, Tasek Gelugor, currently has 61 pig farms.
"Investigations must examine all potential pollution sources, including agricultural activities, waste disposal, drainage systems and other environmental factors.

"We are coordinating monitoring, inspections and enforcement with the Penang Department of Environment, local authorities, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage and other relevant agencies to identify the actual causes and ensure compliance with existing laws," H'ng said today.

The state Veterinary Services Department has put in place the Pig Farming Enactment 2016 and the Pig Farming Regulations (Penang) 2020, with monitoring covering closed-house farming systems, wastewater treatment and effluent discharged from treatment ponds.
H'ng said a multi-agency meeting on May 11 had outlined short- and long-term measures to improve waste management.
Under the immediate plan, solid and liquid waste from farms in Kampung Selamat is transported to a biogas plant in Ampang Jajar.
Waste from farms in Seberang Prai Tengah has been sent to the Kampung Valdor biogas plant since June 2026, while arrangements in Seberang Prai Selatan began in 2023.
A biogas facility has also been proposed for Kampung Selamat to provide a more sustainable, long-term solution.
Separately, H'ng said cleaning works at Parit Cina and Sungai Kereh were expected to begin in the first quarter of next year to remove accumulated sediment and improve water flow.

"The state will take enforcement action against those found violating regulations," he said, adding that the industry's economic contribution must not come at the expense of environmental protection and residents' well-being.
He said Penang would continue pursuing coordinated, practical solutions through modern technology, effective waste treatment and stricter enforcement.
Pollution in Sungai Kereh has been a longstanding problem, dating back as far as four decades.
Numerous protests have been held over the years against the worsening situation.

ebe3bb15af4d14dc: KUALA LUMPUR: Taobao Tmall World is stepping up its global cross-border shopping strategy, sharpening its focus on distinctive Chinese brands and quality products as international consumers increasingly look beyond low prices for items that reflect their personal tastes.

The platform is upgrading its shopping experience with artificial intelligence (AI)-powered recommendations, curated product selections and improved logistics, seeking to turn its vast Chinese merchandise catalogue into a stronger draw for overseas shoppers.

The move comes as demand for original Chinese products, including designer toys, fashion, homeware and smart electronics, gains traction globally alongside the growing international popularity of Chinese dramas, animation and games.
In a statement, Taobao said cross-border shopping preferences were shifting from price-driven purchases towards quality, distinctiveness and personalisation.

Its data from the 2025 Double 11 shopping festival showed that the number of cross-border users buying higher-priced items had increased significantly, with shoppers spending more than RMB500 per order rising 10 per cent year-on-year.

The trend points to an opportunity for Taobao to capture greater spending by making it easier for international customers to discover original Chinese brands and products that may be difficult to find in their home markets.

To support the strategy, the platform is drawing on a catalogue of more than three billion products available for cross-border purchase, backed by its cross-border logistics network and localised services.

Taobao Tmall World general manager Ye Tian said the platform's competitive advantage lay in combining its extensive product range with competitive pricing, trusted logistics and services tailored to individual markets.
"Responding to users' increasingly evolving expectations, we have launched an upgrade across six refreshed user experiences this year," Ye said.

The revamp is intended to make product discovery more intuitive while helping consumers navigate a catalogue spanning apparel, accessories, home furnishings, electronics, pet supplies, designer toys, and sports and outdoor equipment.

The company said its product-selection strength was supported by China's manufacturing supply chain and broad merchant ecosystem, enabling it to offer both everyday essentials and niche products linked to fast-moving consumer trends.

The platform has also observed international travellers using Taobao while visiting China to purchase distinctive products and arrange delivery directly to their hotels, reflecting growing interest in merchandise that is less readily available in their home markets.

f3d2ee259e680e74: BENGALURU: Uefa has sent a letter to Fifa seeking answers about Gianni Infantino's presidency, including questions over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and the Fifa Peace Prize, by Nov 2, British media reported on Monday.

Uefa has led calls for Infantino to resign since he proposed the now-abandoned FFE project, which involved creating a company to run the commercial interests of Fifa competitions, including the World Cup, and selling a minority stake to private investors.

The 56-year-old, who is up for reelection next year, apologised to the Fifa Council last week and told attendees to submit any questions they had about his governance in writing so he could answer them at the next meeting on Dec 16.

However, Sky Sports and other British media reported on Monday that Uefa General Secretary Theodore Theodoridis had written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom seeking a swift response to 42 questions covering 12 topics.
"These questions require answers now," Theodoridis wrote.
"They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the Fifa Council - nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them."
Reuters has not seen a copy of the letter.
Uefa and Fifa did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
Infantino will stand for reelection in March 2027, with a Nov 18 deadline looming for potential candidates to submit their nominations.
8c1091ad2f30bbf9: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should implement its institutional reform agenda more comprehensively and transparently, said former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin.

"In this regard, I welcome the government's firm commitment to implementing the recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Tabung Haji, which was established during my tenure as prime minister.

"I also welcome any steps to review reports of financial leakages involving institutions related to Felda and other bodies in the future," he said when debating the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
On the prosecution of individuals linked to the Tabung Haji case, Muhyiddin said he hoped the principle of innocence until proven guilty would be respected.
"Give them the opportunity to defend themselves in an independent court and respect the independence of the judiciary in upholding justice," he said.
Meanwhile, Muhyiddin proposed that the government develop a five-year national blueprint to address poverty in urban and semi-urban areas.

"The National Urban Poverty Eradication Master Plan, involving agencies across ministries, should focus specifically on housing, healthcare, employment, education, skills training, social assistance and other areas that often pose challenges to the urban poor," he said.

He said the urban absolute poverty rate stood at 3.7 per cent in 2024, down from 4.5 per cent in 2022. However, relative poverty remained high at 16.7 per cent, highlighting persistent challenges related to inequality and the cost of living, including in urban areas.

"All forms of development in major urban centres such as Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Johor Baru and other cities must incorporate plans to address urban poverty, with the aim of lifting the poor out of poverty permanently.

"Rapid development in major urban centres must not place greater pressure on or marginalise the poor. Specific plans must be put in place to ensure the urban poor have access to economic and educational opportunities to improve their lives and those of their families and benefit from the spillover effects of urban development," he said.

154916c3281e325d: KUALA LUMPUR: A former senior manager at Tabung Haji (TH) is seeking to quash his conviction for corruption over a RM170,477 bribe he received more than 10 years ago.
Zaharuddin Hamid was found guilty by the sessions court on Nov 30, 2023, on three counts of graft involving RM170,477 received through a company from a man named Yusaidi Mohd.
The court sentenced him to three years’ imprisonment for each of the three charges, to be served concurrently, and fined him RM852,385, with an additional 15 months’ imprisonment if he failed to pay.

The money, deposited into his sister's account, was intended as an inducement to help two construction firms secure renovation contracts at TH's offices in Ipoh, Perak, and in Muar, Batu Pahat and Kluang, Johor.
According to the facts of the case, Zaharuddin met with Yusaidi and another individual at a restaurant sometime in 2015 to discuss the renovation tender.
The sessions court was told that during the meeting, Zaharuddin demanded a 2% cut from Yusaidi with the payment to be made in two tranches.
Zaharuddin denied this. The court ruled that his defence amounted to a bare denial and failed to rebut the statutory presumption invoked.
Zaharuddin was granted bail pending the disposal of his appeal.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Nurdin fixed Jan 20 for the hearing of Zaharuddin's appeal during case management today.
Zaharuddin was represented by Ashok Athimulan while deputy public prosecutor Haresh Prakash Somiah appeared for the prosecution.
2f59fb9a3c6a8a08: PETALING JAYA: Menteri Besar Selangor Amirudin Shari berkata, beliau akan mengkaji semula rancangan kerjasama kerajaan negeri dengan Bersatu susulan pembatalan pendaftaran Perikatan Nasional (PN), namun menegaskan persefahaman itu dibuat bersama Bersatu, bukannya gabungan itu.
