c8b406fe1826ec02: KUALA LUMPUR: Power infrastructure engineering solutions provider SKA Capital Bhd has set its initial public offering (IPO) price at 43 sen a share ahead of its listing on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market on Nov 11.
The IPO comprises a public issue of 168.08 million new shares to raise RM72.3 million for the company.
This is alongside an offer for sale of 72.4 million existing shares through a private placement to selected investors.

Of the new shares, 44.78 million will be made available to the Malaysian public, while 8.96 million will be allocated to eligible directors, employees and individuals who have contributed to the company.
Another 111.94 million shares will be placed with Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, while 2.41 million shares will be placed with selected investors.
The 72.4 million existing shares under the offer for sale will also be placed with selected investors.
Based on its enlarged share capital of 895.5 million shares, SKA Capital is expected to have a market capitalisation of RM385.1 million upon listing.
The company said proceeds will be used mainly to buy machinery and equipment, support performance bond requirements for future projects and fund working capital.

"This will enhance the group's ability to undertake multiple projects concurrently and compete for larger, higher-value power infrastructure contracts. The balance will be used to defray listing expenses," it said.
SKA Capital managing director Datuk Subas Kumar A/L Ambairam said the listing will strengthen its financial position and execution capacity.
This will allowing the company to undertake multiple projects concurrently and pursue larger, more complex power infrastructure contracts.

"We intend to build on our project track record, industry credentials and established customer relationships to replenish our order book and deepen our participation in power infrastructure projects across Peninsular Malaysia.

SKA Capital provides substation engineering services, including engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning, civil and structural engineering, electrical and mechanical engineering, underground utilities engineering, and the trading of electrical equipment and construction materials.
TA Securities Holdings Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO.
f808db446c674ad6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has urged the government to recognise femicide in the country’s legal framework. It described femicide as the most extreme form of gender-based violence against women and girls.

“Such violence extends beyond individual acts of criminal conduct and reflects broader patterns of discrimination, gender inequality and shortcomings in preventing and addressing violence against women and girls,” it said in a statement today.
The commission described femicide as “a preventable human rights violation requiring stronger laws, early intervention, accessible protection mechanisms and coordinated action”.
“Recognising their gender-related nature is essential to understanding the underlying causes, identifying risks and strengthening prevention, protection and accountability measures,” it said.
The call follows a briefing on October 15 by Suhakam commissioner Melissa Mohd Akhir to the Parliamentary Select Committee on Women, Children and Community Development.
The committee is chaired by Puchong MP Yeo Bee Yin.
Suhakam said “preventing femicide requires action before violence escalates into the loss of life”.

It called for existing laws to be reviewed so femicide is recognised as a distinct form of gender-based violence. It also asked for a national body to coordinate and monitor efforts against such violence at federal, state and local levels, backed by better data collection.

It also urged safer cities and communities through better street lighting, safer public transport, accessible reporting mechanisms and secure schools. It asked media organisations and digital platforms to curb victim-blaming and content that normalises gender-based violence.
The commission said sufficient funding was needed for shelters, psychosocial services, legal aid and women’s organisations, particularly in rural and underserved communities.

Citing Article 8(2) of the Federal Constitution and Malaysia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Cedaw), Suhakam said the government must pursue a policy of eliminating discrimination against women without delay.

Marking the International Day of the Girl Child this month, the commission said “every woman and girl has the right to live free from violence and fear, and that safeguarding this right is a shared responsibility of the government and society”.

7978f6ed4240eba6: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) and Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) have projected Malaysia's headline inflation to ease to an average of 1.9 per cent in 2026, while Apex Securities Bhd has a slightly lower forecast of 1.8 per cent.

In separate notes today, HLIB lowered its consumer price index (CPI) forecast to 1.9 per cent from 2.0 per cent previously, citing continued petrol subsidies, electricity bill protections and limited pass-through of higher input costs. PublicInvest retained its revised forecast at 1.9 per cent, down from 2.1 per cent previously.

The analysts said Malaysia's headline inflation, which refers to total price changes in an economy, eased to 1.8 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) in September from 1.9 per cent in August. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, remained steady at 1.7 per cent.

HLIB said the moderation was mainly due to softer inflation in housing, utilities, food and beverages, and information and communication, with headline inflation averaging 1.8 per cent in the first nine months of 2026 (9M 2026).

HLIB said inflation in housing, utilities and other fuels eased to 1.4 per cent from 2.1 per cent, partly reflecting a high base effect following a targeted water price increase in September last year, while electricity inflation softened following the expansion of the monthly electricity bill protection threshold from 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) to 800 kWh from Sept 1 to Dec 31, 2026.

It said food inflation moderated to 1.8 per cent from 1.9 per cent as inflation for food at home eased while food away from home edged higher to 2.6 per cent from 2.5 per cent. Transport inflation accelerated to 2.5 per cent from 2.0 per cent.

HLIB also said recent escalation of geopolitical tensions and the lagged impact of El Nino could lead to stronger inflationary pressures, prompting it to maintain its 2027 CPI forecast at 2.1 per cent.

Meanwhile, PublicInvest said underlying price pressures have remained contained, but high oil prices, Gulf shipping disruptions and El-Nino-related food price pressures could push consumer prices higher.

"Targeted fuel subsidies and the temporary expansion of electricity-bill exemptions to 800 kWh should cushion household costs through end-2026," it said. It said persistent input-cost pressures could drive up retail and services inflation.
PublicInvest has projected inflation at 2.3 per cent in 2027. It said Budget 2027 household assistance and income tax relief should support consumption.
But the RM2,000 minimum wage from June 2027 could raise labour costs, notwithstanding exemptions for micro, small and medium enterprises.
Separately, Apex Securities Bhd's external trade research has headline inflation forecasts of 1.8 per cent for 2026 and 2.0 per cent for 2027.

The research house has raised its 2026 export growth forecast to 35.1 per cent from 26.2 per cent, reflecting stronger-than-expected growth momentum in the first nine months of the year. It remains positive on electrical and electronics exports, supported by the global technology upcycle and structural demand for artificial intelligence-related applications.

Nevertheless, Apex Securities said downside risks remained, particularly from prolonged West Asia tensions that could disrupt global trade flows and continued uncertainty surrounding United States trade policy.

af09d0737709053b: KUALA LUMPUR: Muhyiddin Yassin menggesa kerajaan mewujudkan pelan induk khusus bagi menangani kemiskinan di kawasan bandar dan separa bandar dalam tempoh lima tahun akan datang.

Bekas perdana menteri itu berkata pelan berkenaan perlu memberi tumpuan kepada perumahan, kesihatan, pekerjaan, pendidikan dan bantuan sosial, dengan penglibatan agensi merentas kementerian bagi memastikan pelaksanaannya lebih menyeluruh dan berkesan.

“Berdasarkan Laporan Survei Pendapatan Isi Rumah Malaysia dan Negeri 2024, jurang kemiskinan dan pendapatan antara bandar dengan luar bandar masih ketara. Kemiskinan mutlak luar bandar kekal pada 10% pada 2024. Pendapatan median isi rumah luar bandar hanya RM4,588 berbanding RM8,139 di bandar.
“Kemiskinan bandar juga menjadi isu yang semakin meruncing. Kadar kemiskinan mutlak bandar ialah 3.7% pada 2024, menurun daripada 4.5% pada 2022.

“Namun, kemiskinan relatif kekal tinggi pada 16.7%. Ini menunjukkan cabaran ketidaksamaan dan kos sara hidup masih relevan, termasuk dalam konteks bandar,” katanya ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.

Ahli Parlimen Pagoh itu berkata pembangunan pesat di bandar besar seperti Kuala Lumpur, Pulau Pinang dan Johor Bahru perlu dirancang dengan mengambil kira keperluan golongan miskin supaya mereka tidak semakin tertekan atau terpinggir.

“Suatu perancangan khusus hendaklah diadakan untuk memastikan golongan miskin bandar mendapat peluang ekonomi dan pendidikan untuk memajukan diri dan keluarga hasil daripada limpahan pembangunan di kawasan bandar,” katanya.
Bimbang sasaran sara diri beras menurun
Dalam ucapannya, Muhyiddin turut membangkitkan kebimbangan berhubung sasaran kadar sara diri (SSR) beras yang ditetapkan pada 54% bagi 2027, berbanding sasaran sebelumnya 59.9%.
Katanya, sasaran itu menimbulkan persoalan memandangkan pencapaian sebenar pada 2025 ialah 54.3%, sedangkan Rancangan Malaysia Ke-13 menetapkan sasaran SSR beras sebanyak 80% menjelang 2030.
“Kalau nak dianggap ini satu krisis, saya fikir ia sudah satu krisis bagi saya. Kita sudah sampai satu detik kritikal sekarang ini untuk menentukan langkah-langkah lebih tegas dan berani,” katanya.

Beliau mencadangkan penubuhan jawatankuasa khas Kabinet yang dipengerusikan perdana menteri untuk tempoh lima tahun bagi merangka pelan tindakan lebih tegas untuk meningkatkan pengeluaran makanan negara.
Menurutnya, antara isu yang perlu diberi perhatian ialah tanah pertanian yang tidak digunakan serta peningkatan kos input pertanian.
Muhyiddin turut menggesa kerajaan melancarkan semula “Revolusi Hijau” bagi meningkatkan pengeluaran beras dan hasil makanan lain.

“Jangan salah faham macam hijau sebelah sana itu (PAS). Revolusi Hijau maknanya kita galakkan, giatkan dan ambil langkah drastik meningkatkan pengeluaran negara dalam semua hasil yang kita boleh bekalkan,” katanya, dipercayai merujuk secara berseloroh kepada PAS.
Sambut baik tindakan susulan RCI TH

Muhyiddin turut menyambut baik tindakan kerajaan melaksanakan syor Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja (RCI) berkaitan Tabung Haji, namun mengingatkan prinsip seseorang tidak bersalah sehingga dibuktikan bersalah perlu dihormati dalam sebarang prosiding mahkamah.

“Saya menggesa supaya kerajaan melaksanakan agenda reformasi institusi dengan lebih tuntas dan telus serta menguatkuasakan undang-undang secara adil dan saksama tanpa pilih kasih dan tanpa mengira pangkat, warna kulit dan fahaman politik.

“Saya juga mengalu-alukan sebarang langkah yang akan diambil untuk meneliti semula laporan-laporan yang melibatkan ketirisan dalam institusi berkaitan kerajaan seperti Felda dan lain-lain badan pada masa hadapan,” katanya.

Selain itu, Muhyiddin menggesa kerajaan mengambil langkah menyeluruh untuk meningkatkan kadar upah pekerja, termasuk menawarkan insentif kepada industri yang membayar gaji lebih tinggi selaras dengan kelayakan dan kemahiran pekerja, khususnya dalam bidang teknologi tinggi.
1c2395afa206e65f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Fares for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link are expected to be announced by the end of this year, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
The announcement will be made ahead of the service’s planned opening in February next year.
“The announcement would be made jointly with RTS Operations (RTSO), as the project was a bilateral initiative between Malaysia and Singapore.
“I cannot make any unilateral announcement because it is a bilateral project,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Exhibition (TXA) here today.
He said the fare announcement would be made before the service begins operating to give the public sufficient time to familiarise themselves with the ticket prices.

In a joint statement made on October 2, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore and the Malaysian Transport Ministry said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline.
The service was previously expected to commence in January. The new target is subject to RTSO obtaining independent safety certification for the RTS Link and securing final regulatory approvals.
e3369362292f1423: SINGAPORE, Oct 20 — Indonesian paper Asia Pulp & Paper (APP) has been placed under temporary green certification restrictions by the Singapore Environment Council (SEC).

The firm, which is behind household tissue and paper towel brand Paseo, was issued a notice of temporary restrictions on its enhanced Singapore Green Labelling Scheme (SGLS+) on Oct 18, after three of its wood-fibre suppliers were linked to ongoing wildfires in Indonesia that have blanketed several South-east Asian nations in hazardous haze.
SEC said in a statement on Monday (Oct 19) that they take a serious view of the harmful impact of haze on the health of people in Singapore and the wider region, as well as on the environment.

Under the notice, APP is required to provide daily fire response reporting and strict monitoring to ensure effective fire prevention and suppression, for the concession areas managed by PT Bumi Mekar Hijau, PT Bumi Andalas Permai, and PT Sebangun Bumi Andalas (SBA) Wood Industries.
The three firms are among seven entities issued with Preventive Measure Notices under Singapore’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act on Oct 16.
SEC’s SGLS+ certification for pulp and paper products was launched in 2017, two years after the severe regional haze episode in 2015.

It incorporated requirements to reduce fire risks on agroforestry plantations, including sustainable peatland management, robust fire prevention, and strict zero-burning compliance throughout the supply chain.
According to SEC, about 58 pulp and paper products, such as printing paper and hygiene paper, are now certified under the scheme.

The council stated that if APP’s additional reporting does not demonstrate that strengthened monitoring, fire prevention and suppression measures are implemented effectively, its SGLS+ certificate may be suspended.
This means that it will not be able to use the SGLS+ logo on products associated with the certification.

And while non-SGLS+ products are not banned from being sold, major local supermarket chains and retailers are known to have pulled such products from shelves when manufacturers loses or fails to achieve the certification.

SEC said it has also asked SGLS+ certified companies to check their supply chains and declare whether they source or purchase wood, paper, and pulp products from any of the entities served with the prevention measure notices.
A total of ten Indonesian firms — seven on Oct 16, and another three on Oct 19 — have since been served with Preventive Measure Notices.

The council also reminded consumers that their daily purchasing decisions can influence companies’ environmental practices, and that they can make a difference by choosing products carefully by looking for the Singapore Green Label where applicable. — AsiaOne
c89e3665a193579c: KUALA LUMPUR: Passengers will enjoy a 30% discount on economy-class tickets for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) during its first month of operations.

The discount is separate from the permanent concessions announced for eligible passengers yesterday. These include a 50% discount for children aged two to 12, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and government pensioners, as well as a 40% discount for students aged 13 to 24.
ECRL tickets will go on sale in mid-November, with one-way fares from Gombak to Kota Bharu starting at RM125 for transit services and RM147 for express services.
Transport minister Loke Siew Fook said the introductory offer would coincide with the launch of the ECRL, with passenger services scheduled to begin on Dec 12.
"So this is meant for members of the public who do not enjoy any ticket concessions," he told a press conference at the Transport Expo Asia 2026 here today.

Loke said the government had considered both affordability for passengers and the financial sustainability of the rail operator when setting fares. He expressed hope that the fares would be well received by the public.
On freight services, Loke said operations between Gombak and Kota Bharu are expected to begin alongside passenger services.
"Freight services connecting to Port Klang will take approximately another year to be completed, as construction of the section between Gombak and Port Klang is still ongoing.
"MRL (Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd) will review freight charges in due course," he added.
On a separate matter, Loke said the Cabinet had approved the proposed 32km extension of the ECRL from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, near the Malaysia-Thailand border.
He said the project is undergoing technical assessment and land acquisition, and is expected to take about four-and-a-half years to complete.
Land will need to be acquired from the state government and private landowners before construction can begin, he added.
72afbb143e7fd650: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government’s policy to channel bus ticket sales through licensed terminals is meant to restrict online ticketing agents (OTA).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said operators needed to understand the policy and there will be a session to explain it to them.
“The policy is not intended to cause losses to bus companies.
“What we want to restrict is the role of online ticketing agents (OTAs), many of which are based overseas.
“They sell tickets and collect commissions but do not provide services at the terminals or manage terminal operations,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Expo Asia 2026 here today.
He cited situations when a problem relating to cancellation or delay in bus services, the ministry is not able to regulate these issues.
“When problems arise, such as service failures or refund disputes, we have limited ability to regulate these agents.
“We are introducing this measure to ensure ticket sales, terminal management and ticketing operations are better regulated,” he added.
Loke stressed that there should be no financial losses for bus operators, at the same time ensuring that terminals cannot charge more than their existing rates.
“In fact, we hope terminals can reduce their charges and provide better returns for bus operators,” he said.
In this case, Loke said, transactions will be business-to-business (B2B), between the terminals and bus operators.
“The government is responsible for the policy decision, while the commercial arrangements will be handled directly by the parties involved.
Loke’s comments come after a new ruling by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) was announced whereby express bus tickets were to be sold only through licensed terminals from November 1.
According to the circular issued to bus operators, it involves granting terminals exclusive rights to sell tickets and introduce new commercial fee structure.
However, APAD said tickets could still be purchased through OTAs or bus operators' websites if the terminals were owned by the operators themselves.
d97e3475e24c1ac8: PETALING JAYA: Bekas Ahli Parlimen Klang Charles Santiago hari ini mengkritik Ahli Parlimen Putrajaya Radzi Jidin kerana cuba 'mencari publisiti' apabila menggesa supaya operasi membanteras pendatang tanpa dokumen di seluruh negara dilaksanakan dengan melibatkan tentera.

Santiago berkata, pekerja migran bukan punca masalah pendatang tanpa izin (Pati) di negara ini, sebaliknya berpunca daripada 'ketamakan, rasuah, pengambilan pekerja secara eksploitatif dan majikan yang tidak bertanggungjawab'.
“Kita terus menyalahkan pekerja, sedangkan pihak yang mengaut keuntungan daripada eksploitasi dibiarkan beroperasi tanpa dikenakan tindakan.

“Ahli Parlimen seperti Radzi perlu memahami isu yang diperkatakan mereka dan bukannya mencari publisiti. Malaysia berulang kali berdepan penelitian antarabangsa dan menanggung malu akibat kelemahan tadbir urus migrasi buruh.
“Kita tidak boleh menyelesaikan masalah dengan menghantar pulang pendatang semata-mata sedangkan kita sendiri gagal mentadbir sistem ini,” katanya dalam beberapa hantaran di X.

Ketika perbahasan Rang Undang-Undang Perbekalan 2027 semalam, Radzi mencadangkan supaya anggota tentera digerakkan bagi membantu Jabatan Imigresen menahan dan menghantar pulang pendatang tanpa dokumen.
Malaysiakini yang memetiknya sebagai berkata, langkah itu akan menghantar mesej jelas kepada masyarakat antarabangsa dan sindiket pemerdagangan manusia bahawa Malaysia serius menangani isu berkenaan.
Radzi turut berkata negara akan 'musnah' jika kerajaan gagal membendung kemasukan Pati secara berkesan, termasuk dengan mengenakan dasar lebih ketat terhadap pengambilan pekerja migran.

Bagaimanapun, Santiago berkata jika tentera dikerahkan, mereka sepatutnya ditugaskan untuk membanteras 'kartel perekrutan yang mewujudkan perhambaan hutang serta pegawai korup yang membolehkan pemerdagangan buruh berlaku'.

Beliau mendakwa undang-undang Malaysia menetapkan had yuran pengambilan pekerja pada kadar sebulan gaji, iaitu RM1,700, tetapi pekerja Bangladesh lazimnya membayar yuran antara RM20,000 hingga RM30,000.
“Jumlah itu bersamaan 12 hingga 17 kali ganda had yang dibenarkan undang-undang, sekali gus memaksa pekerja tinggal lebih masa untuk mendapatkan semula wang yang dibayar.

“Jika kita serius mahu mengurangkan migrasi tidak teratur, kita mesti meruntuhkan sistem yuran perekrutan yang menguntungkan itu, yang menjana keuntungan besar dengan mengorbankan pekerja migran dan mengekalkan kitaran perhambaan hutang,” katanya.
d9b44b1fe4ee4ce2: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal increased the damages payable by five defendants to an estate company to RM449,256.20 after upholding a finding that they conspired to make unlawful profits from a contract for estate operations.

A three-member bench comprising Justices Zaini Mazlan, Faizah Jamaludin and Aliza Sulaiman allowed the relevant appeals in the dispute involving Syarikat V K Kalyanasundram Sdn Bhd, the owner of Huntly Estate and manager of VKK Estate.

The company sued its director and managing director, Kalyani Balasubramaniam; former director and general manager, Barani Kumar Balasubramaniam; directors Vijay Anand P Harivasagan and Thulasingam Kaliappan; and Cosmos Resources Sdn Bhd.
On Aug 1, 2024, the High Court found the five defendants liable for conspiracy and awarded RM260,724 in damages jointly and severally.
The Court of Appeal reassessed the losses proven and increased the award to RM449,256.20.
The dispute arose from a 10-year agreement signed on Feb 3, 2021, under which Cosmos Resources was appointed to provide workers and harvesting and transportation services.

The company alleged that Cosmos Resources, a newly incorporated entity without its own workforce, was interposed between the estate and existing contractors, allowing it to retain substantial margins following revisions to service rates.
Payments allegedly channelled through Thulasingam to Kalyani, Barani and Vijay were disguised as salaries or loan repayments.

Faizah, who delivered the judgment, said the company's failure to establish fraud or prove that the agreement was a sham did not defeat its separate claims of conspiracy by unlawful means and breaches of duty.
The court set aside the finding of conspiracy by lawful means but upheld the finding of conspiracy by unlawful means against the five defendants.
The bench also affirmed findings that Kalyani and Vijay breached their fiduciary duties, while Barani breached his contractual duty.
Claims against two other defendants, Jeraman Narainan and Bhoo Pathy Ramakrishnan, were dismissed by the High Court, and the company abandoned its appeals against them.
Ranjit Singh and Navpreet Singh appeared for the company while K Shanmuga represented the five defendants. Lai Choe Ken acted for Jeraman and Bhoo Pathy.
00d8b920dcd4cf6b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said his attendance at national songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza’s concert recently was by special invitation and also in support of efforts to promote local arts, heritage and culture.
Responding to criticism from several quarters over his attendance, Anwar thanked them and said he accepted their views with an open heart, according to a report by national news agency Bernama today.

“I went because Siti Nurhaliza and her husband, Datuk K (Datuk Seri Khalid Mohamad Jiwa), really urged me to attend, although I arrived a little late... but I was criticised by several quarters. Thank you,” he said during Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar was responding to a joke by Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) about his attendance at the Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara, held at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil last Saturday.
The prime minister said the concert by the country’s renowned singer deserved praise for elevating the nation’s cultural heritage through its various traditional elements.

He said the traditional concert showcased the beauty of the country’s artistic heritage through wayang kulit, traditional dances and cultural performances from Sabah and Sarawak, highlighting the richness of local heritage and classical songs.
bc2acd879f936464: PETALING JAYA: Seorang murid berusia tujuh tahun dilaporkan maut selepas dipercayai mengalami kesukaran bernafas ketika berada di dalam kelas di sebuah sekolah di Dengkil semalam.
Ketua Polis Sepang Norhizam Bahaman berkata, pihaknya menerima laporan berhubung kejadian pada 7.30 malam semalam.
“Mangsa dilaporkan mengalami kesukaran bernafas ketika berada di dalam kelas sebelum diberikan bantuan awal pernafasan di lokasi kejadian," katanya dalam kenyataan, lapor Bernama.
Norhizam berkata, bedah siasat telah dijalankan di Hospital Putrajaya pada 8 pagi tadi dan kes diklasifikasikan sebagai kematian mengejut.

Menurutnya, siasatan lanjut berhubung kejadian sedang dijalankan oleh Bahagian Siasatan Jenayah IPD Sepang dan beliau meminta pihak mempunyai maklumat menghubungi pegawai penyiasat T Vishno Kumar menerusi talian 011-11021528 bagi membantu siasatan.
Norhizam turut menasihati orang ramai agar tidak menyebarkan maklumat tidak benar berhubung kejadian berkenaan.
Terdahulu, tular insiden murid Tahun Satu SK Dengkil didakwa tercekik makanan, namun tidak berjaya diselamatkan.
9ff065c3cc7cf3b9: Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.
The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.

The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan's flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan's heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.
b1095b27208fb0b6: PETALING JAYA: Selangor menteri besar Amirudin Shari says he will review the state government’s planned cooperation with Bersatu following the deregistration of Perikatan Nasional (PN), but insists the arrangement is with Bersatu and not PN.
Speaking to reporters in Shah Alam, he said the position of the cooperation would be decided "in a day or two".
"We are not sure (about PN's status). I need to check first. Perhaps in a day or two, we will determine the status of the cooperation with Bersatu," he was quoted as saying by Astro Awani.
"As for the cancellation of PN's registration, that is an internal problem which they must resolve themselves. Because our plan is with Bersatu, not PN."
Amirudin, a PKR vice-president, said the agreement between the state government and Bersatu is expected to be signed next week, subject to confirmation.
"I will have to wait for confirmation first, perhaps after the 25th or 26th," he said.
The Selangor government has been negotiating a pact with Bersatu in the hope of sealing it before the state budget is tabled in November.
The proposed deal comes amid growing tensions between Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional (BN) in Selangor, as well as strain within PN, where PAS has emerged as the dominant partner.
The 56-member Selangor assembly comprises 32 assemblymen from PH, 11 from Bersatu, 10 from PAS, two from BN and one independent.
A deal with Bersatu would give Amirudin the support of more than two-thirds of the assembly.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS) deregistered PN today after finding that the coalition's response to a show-cause notice failed to justify retaining its registration.
After examining the documents and explanations provided by PN on Oct 12, the RoS found that PN failed to rebut the grounds for revoking its registration.
PN subsequently said it would challenge the deregistration and seek a stay of the move.
3783e06ce85a7d88: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional (PN) mempertimbangkan untuk merayu kepada menteri dalam negeri susulan keputusan Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan (JPPM) membatalkan pendaftaran gabungan itu.
Setiausaha Agung Takiyuddin Hassan berkata pendekatan itu antara yang dipertimbang oleh PN bagi mencabar tindakan JPPM selain daripada proses perundangan.
"Akta Pertubuhan 1966 membenarkan pihak terkilan merayu kepada menteri dalam tempoh 30 hari daripada keputusan JPPM.
"PN akan meneliti semua tindakan yang boleh diambil di mahkamah dan peringkat pentadbiran," katanya pada sidang media di Parlimen.
Awal hari ini, JPPM mengumumkan pembatalan pendaftaran PN selepas mendapati penjelasan dikemukakan gabungan itu gagal menyangkal asas pembatalan dalam notis terdahulu.
Jabatan itu berkata keputusan dibuat selepas meneliti dokumen dan penjelasan PN yang diterima pada 12 Okt, yang didapati tidak memberikan justifikasi kukuh untuk mengekalkan pendaftarannya.
Pembatalan itu dibuat mengikut subperenggan 13(1)(c)(iv) Akta Pertubuhan 1966.

Siasatan JPPM terhadap PN dibuat susulan aduan dilaporkan Bersatu yang mendakwa mereka dinafikan hak untuk menghadiri, memberi pendapat dan mengundi di dalam mesyuarat Majlis Tertinggi PN pada 16 Jul.
PN sebelum ini memfailkan permohonan semakan kehakiman pada 5 Okt bagi mencabar notis JPPM, sebelum mendapat kebenaran memulakan prosiding berkenaan pada 13 Okt.
Bagaimanapun, mahkamah tidak membenarkan penangguhan sementara terhadap penggantungan aktiviti PN. Pendengaran permohonan penangguhan dengan kehadiran kedua-dua pihak ditetapkan pada 22 Okt.
Takiyuddin turut menjelaskan PN masih boleh bertanding pada PRN Melaka, 14 Nov ini, menggunakan logo parti anggotanya walaupun pendaftaran gabungan itu dibatalkan.
Bagaimanapun, beliau berkata parti anggota PN belum memutuskan logo yang akan digunakan dan perkara itu akan dibincangkan bersama.
“Kita belum lagi buat keputusan logo apa yang kita akan gunakan,” katanya.
Takiyuddin turut mendakwa pembatalan pendaftaran PN menjejaskan hak lebih 600,000 pengundi Melaka untuk memilih gabungan itu pada PRN akan datang.
“Mereka seolah-olah dinafikan pilihan kepada mereka untuk memilih PN,” katanya.
f87c39b5004a7b22: SEGAMAT, Oct 20 — A businessman has claimed that a fake Facebook account, using his name and image, was used to post content insulting the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Malay community.
Segamat police chief Superintendent Mohd Jumazanzahir Chek Ismail said that the complainant, a local man, lodged a police report here the day before yesterday.
“Police confirm having received a report regarding the misuse of his personal information to create a fake Facebook account.
“This account used his name and photo to upload posts involving 3R (religion, race, and the royal institution) issues,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Jumazanzahir said the complainant has denied that the Facebook account belongs to him and maintains that he never posted the content in question.

“He believes his personal information was misused, creating the false impression that he was the individual responsible for publishing such content," he said, adding that two police reports have been filed in this district, with another lodged in the Shah Alam, all related to the issue.

Meanwhile, Mohd Jumazanzahir advised the public against misusing the identities or personal information of others for fake accounts, disseminating seditious content, or inciting misunderstandings within the community.

“The public is also advised to refrain from speculating or resharing content that has not been verified, particularly content that touches upon sensitive issues regarding race, religion, and the royal institution," he said.

Previously, a post circulating on social media, using the name Cher Cher, had insulted the Yang di-Pertuan Agong through the use of edited content, accompanied by a caption insulting the Malay community.
683a1a718ec5ed53: SYDNEY: Australian lawmakers and enforcers have to sought to lower the temperature of political debate and warned about growing threats to public figures since 2021, when anti-lockdown protesters put an effigy of a state leader on a makeshift gallows in Melbourne.

Those fears came to a head on Monday when a man rammed a car into Helen Haines, an independent member of the lower-house, inflicting major injuries including the loss of a leg, media and officials said, while doctors work to save the other.
Police have yet to state a motive for the attack outside Haines' regional electorate office in Wangaratta, some 240km (150 miles) away from Melbourne.
"We've all seen a level of ... hate and disrespect and intolerance in our political debate that we never really used to see," Health minister Mark Butler told Channel Nine's Today Show.

His remarks come amid growing debate about increasingly toxic political dialogue in a country that has traditionally prized easy access to politicians who usually live in their electorates among minimal security.
Threats of violence to politicians were "increasing, not decreasing", said Bridget McKenzie, a senator from the opposition Nationals who has an office in Haines's electorate.
"Everybody, no matter where they come from in parliament, left or right, is doing their very, very best to make our country the best. We disagree on the way to do it."
Threats to lawmakers on the rise

As many as 85% of federal lawmakers and their staffers had experienced violent, threatening or volatile behaviour, a 2025 parliamentary report showed, calling for more consistent security arrangements.
The incidents occurred more than once a month, said nearly half of the respondents cited in the report, who described assaults, spitting, threats, intimidation and objects thrown at them.

"You worry about your family, you worry about the impact of this on whether you can actually continue to do your job," said Lisa Phillips, a psychological sciences professor at Melbourne University who published a 2023 paper on threats to members of the Victorian state parliament.
"It's distressing," added Phillips, whose paper found 85% of state lawmakers had made lifestyle changes after threats of harm, with female politicians more likely to be abused than men.
The warnings stretch back years.
Security environment 'volatile'
In 2021, Mike Burgess, the head of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation, warned of "considerable volatility" in security stemming from the Covid-19 pandemic.
Such conditions fuelled grievance-driven extremism and heightened the risk of lone-actor violence, Burgess added.
Australian politicians were spurred to openly discuss their own vulnerability seven months later, when British MP David Amess was fatally stabbed while meeting constituents.
By 2024, there was a surge in reports of threats, harassment and offensive communications targeting federal politicians.
Politically motivated violence was "flashing red", Burgess said in 2025, stepping up his warning.

In February, a bomb threat prompted the evacuation of prime minister Anthony Albanese from his official residence, while small businesses minister Anne Aly said she had received 19 death threats in a single week.

Australian Federal Police figures showed 1,067 reports of threats, harassment, nuisance or offensive behaviour against parliamentarians, senior officeholders and protected locations in the latest financial year.
That was up 12% on the prior year and double the figure from five years earlier.
"ASIO has seen direct correlations between inflamed language, inflamed tensions and acts of violence," Burgess said on Tuesday.
"The temperature of our security environment would be several degrees lower if we recommitted to conversing with civility, debating with respect and disagreeing with restraint."
41d30ad121fc1bee: WANGARATTA (Australia), Oct 20 — Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has lost a leg after being struck by a car in a deliberate attack, local media said Tuesday.
Political violence is rare in Australia, but law enforcement have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards the nation’s elected officials in recent years.

Prime Minister Albanese said the attack was a “test of our character” and led an outpouring of support for Haines, widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.
She was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres (124 miles) northeast of Melbourne, at around 3.35pm on Monday.
Witnesses told national broadcaster ABC they heard a bang and saw a woman pinned between two cars.
She was getting things from the trunk of her car when the attack happened, Albanese said.
The driver did a U-turn to get back to her after passing, he added.
“It’s clear this was a deliberate act,” he said.
‘Hero’ barber
The 65-year-old was critically injured.
She underwent surgery overnight at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne.
National broadcaster ABC and the Sydney Morning Herald reported she had lost a leg.
“Helen remains in hospital in a critical condition. I spoke with her husband Phil last night, and she underwent surgery last night,” Albanese told Australian breakfast show Sunrise.
“All Australians’ thoughts are with the family, with her many friends, with her community,” he added.
The 43-year-old male driver of the vehicle was restrained by local barber Ricky Jefferies—now widely hailed as a “hero”.
Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: “my wife would be disappointed if I’m injured”.
“My family, they’re everything, and my community is second to that,” a visibly shaken Jefferies told journalists.
“The other people here were just, they did so much more than me... they deserve the credit.”
‘Devastating’
The driver was then arrested and police found a knife in his car.
Australian media reported that he was known to police and that his name is Brendan Nugent.
An investigation by federal police, the counter-terrorism squad and Victoria state law enforcement is ongoing and he remained in custody on Tuesday morning.

Federal police said they were working with local law enforcement on possible charges, including the offence of causing harm to a government official — which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years’ imprisonment.
The alleged attacker’s motive remains unknown and Albanese has refused to speculate while the investigation takes place.
But he has bemoaned the fact that political debate in Australia had grown too heated and personal over the past few years and pointed to a significant increase in threats against elected officials.
“It’s important in a democracy that people are allowed to have disagreements,” he said.
“But that doesn’t mean that you have to draw into question people’s motivations or their patriotism or who they are.”
“We’ve seen, I think, political discourse go in the wrong direction in recent times,” he said.
Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action.
“This afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care,” her family said.
“We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response.”
Tributes to the independent lawmaker have poured in from across the political spectrum.
Conservative opposition leader Angus Taylor described it as a “shocking day for our nation”.
And far-right Senator Pauline Hanson said “violence against any elected representative, whoever they are and whatever they stand for, is never acceptable in Australia”. — AFP
bd40dd3f364b402b: Projection delivers a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin a process toward independence, the national broadcaster CBC has projected, delivering a victory for the prime minister, Mark Carney, and supporters of Canadian unity. With more than 1m votes counted early on Tuesday, about 76% supported remaining in Canada, compared with 23% who backed beginning a process that could lead to separation. About a third of ballots had been counted. Continue reading...
f8b4f6aa85affd3b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the cancellation of Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) registration showed that the coalition’s leadership, led by PAS, had breached the Societies Act 1966 and PN’s constitution.

In a statement posted on Facebook today, Azmin said the explanations and evidence provided by PAS during the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) investigation were baseless and failed to meet legal and constitutional requirements.

He said the PN leadership’s decision to deny Bersatu the right to attend, express its views and vote at a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16 amounted to a serious breach of Clause 7.1 of the coalition’s constitution.
Azmin said the action had caused significant harm to PN and could jeopardise its future.

He also accused the coalition’s leadership of disregarding good governance and transparency, creating pressure to remove Bersatu’s membership through a veto exercised by an individual who did not hold a position on the PN Supreme Council.

Azmin said Bersatu had been called to give evidence to the RoS on August 18 and had provided factual explanations and evidence that PN’s leadership had denied the party rights guaranteed under the coalition’s constitution.
He said Bersatu’s complaint, submitted on August 11, was intended to ensure PN was managed with accountability, transparency and integrity, and complied with the law and its constitution.

“PN cannot be allowed to become a shelter for groups hungry for political power and seeking to hijack the Perikatan Nasional brand, which is moderate, progressive and responsive to the Malaysian people,” he said.
Azmin accused PAS and its allies of portraying themselves as victims of political manoeuvring to gain sympathy ahead of the Melaka state election.

He also criticised what he described as excessive identity politics, accusing PAS of failing to manage an organisation based on democratic principles and good governance, and of betraying its political allies.
Azmin said Bersatu found the RoS decision difficult to accept because it was a founding member of PN and had helped establish the coalition.

Nevertheless, he said Bersatu accepted that PN must fulfil its responsibilities under its constitution and the Societies Act 1966, also known as Act 832, to ensure legal compliance and orderly governance.

He said Bersatu would study the full RoS decision before its Supreme Leadership Council discussed the next steps to rebuild public confidence in a political coalition that promotes moderation, values-based politics and a new vision for a prosperous Malaysia.
6a0d136970b1b39d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will challenge the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to cancel the coalition’s registration, including by appealing to the home minister, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today.
He said the legal challenge would begin with an application during the Kuala Lumpur High Court hearing of PN’s application for a stay on Thursday.
Takiyuddin said Section 18 of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832) allows any local society, office-bearer, member or aggrieved party to appeal against a decision by the RoS to the Home Minister.

The appeal must be filed within 30 days of the RoS decision, he said, adding that Section 8 of the same Act empowers the Home Minister to confirm, reject or amend the Registrar’s decision, with the minister’s decision being final.
“PN will challenge the validity of the Cancellation Order and seek a stay of its implementation and all its effects pending the court’s determination.

“PN also urges the Attorney General to explain this action in light of the position taken by the Attorney General’s Chambers in court during the hearing of PN’s stay application this Thursday,” he told a press conference at Parliament today.
Takiyuddin said PN would also take action against parties it believed had shown contempt for the court process.
“PN will also take action against all parties that have shown contempt for and disregarded the court process,” he said.
(RoS) cancelled the registration of PN after finding that the explanation submitted by the coalition failed to refute the grounds for deregistration stated in an earlier notice.
RoS said it made the decision after examining all the documents and explanations submitted by PN on October 12.
According to the department, the reasons given by PN also did not provide strong justification for maintaining the party’s registration.
d073b331bfeab7be: In today’s newsletter: The prime minister’s campaign against noisy passengers has struck a chord with commuters. Whether anyone hears him remains to be seen. Good morning. Me again, back from the October school holiday (a week in glorious Wales, thanks for asking) and ready to hear your commuter woes. For our prime minister, it’s “one of the most annoying things on public transport”: maybe you’re trying to work, or read, or you’ve finally got your kid to sleep, when someone starts blasting sound from their phone at full volume. France | The prime minister has said he has asked regional authorities to impose partial curfews in some cities after the government admitted police had “lost control” in several places during violent weekend protests around the country. Yemen | At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government forces in the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September. Reform | Nigel Farage undermined his own claims that a £5m gift was for security when he referred to the money as a reward for Brexit, according to one of his closest aides. Continue reading...
e4cac0f1a255574a: PETALING JAYA: Former Klang MP Charles Santiago today panned Putrajaya MP Radzi Jidin for "playing to the gallery" in his call for a nationwide crackdown on undocumented migrants involving the military.
Santiago said migrant workers were not responsible for the nation’s illegal immigration problems, which he attributed to "greed, corruption, exploitative recruitment and unscrupulous employers".
"We continue to blame the worker while allowing the people who profit from exploitation to operate with impunity.

"MPs like Radzi need to understand the issues they speak about instead of playing to the gallery. Malaysia has repeatedly faced international scrutiny and embarrassment over its poor labour migration governance.
"We simply cannot deport our way out of a system that we have failed to govern," he said in a series of posts on X.
During the debate on the 2027 budget bill yesterday, Radzi proposed mobilising military personnel to help the immigration department arrest and deport undocumented migrants.
Malaysiakini reported him as saying this would send a clear message to the international community and human trafficking syndicates that Malaysia is serious about tackling the issue.

Radzi also said the country would be "destroyed" if the government failed to effectively stem the entry of illegal immigrants, including by imposing stricter policies on the employment of migrant workers.
However, Santiago said if soldiers are deployed, they should be sent against "recruitment cartels that manufacture debt bondage and corrupt officials who enable labour trafficking".
He claimed that while Malaysian law caps worker recruitment fees at one month's wage, or RM1,700, Bangladeshi workers routinely pay fees ranging from RM20,000 to RM30,000.
"That is 12 to 17 times the legal limit, forcing workers to overstay to recoup their payments.

"If we are serious about reducing irregular migration, we must dismantle the lucrative recruitment-fee system that generates mega profits at the expense of migrant workers and perpetuates the cycle of debt bondage," he said.
06f95e38383674da: WASHINGTON, Oct 20 — President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday announced it had finalised a deep-sea mining auction off the coast of American Samoa, the first in the United States’ history, despite widespread opposition from locals and environmental groups.
The lease sales will cover approximately 31 million acres over two areas off the US Pacific archipelago, with bidding set for November 19.

“Critical minerals are no longer just commodities; they are a vital strategic asset in global competition, essential for reaching our energy efficiency goals, strengthening our national defence, and securing domestic supply chains,” said Mike Olsen, acting director for the Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), which falls under the Interior Department, in a statement.

“MMA recognises the ocean floor surrounding American Samoa carries cultural, economic, and environmental significance, requiring that the pursuit of national security and energy readiness is balanced with rigorous environmental stewardship,” he added.

The sale follows an April 2025 executive order in which Trump called leadership in deep-sea science and technology “a core national security and economic interest,” and a request by US firm Impossible Metals to open leasing off the territory, which lies east of the independent nation of Samoa.

Mining companies want to scour the ocean’s abyssal plains for polymetallic nodules laden with nickel, copper and cobalt. Critics fear irreversible damage, with plumes of waste smothering marine life and the thrum of heavy machinery disrupting migrations.
American Samoa banned deep-sea mining in its territorial waters in 2024, but the auction concerns the federally controlled Outer Continental Shelf beyond that limit.

In a public comment submitted in September 2026 about the auction, American Samoa Governor Pulaali’i Nikolao Pula said he “does not support commercial deep-sea mineral extraction at this time” but acknowledged the final decision rests with the US government.
“These lease sales will open the floodgates to the exploitation of our deep seas,” said Oceana Defense Campaign Manager Julia Singer.

“The message from American Samoa, and people across the United States, could not be clearer: stop deep-sea mining before it starts. Thousands of scientists, local leaders, and community members have warned of the danger that deep-sea mining poses, yet the Trump administration is continuing to ignore widespread opposition to this proposal. The US government should defend the deep, not fast-track its destruction.”
The area borders the vast Rose Atoll marine sanctuary, where endangered species of hawksbill turtle thrive on vibrant reefs. — AFP
101a659b2e2a7413: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Transport Ministry is in the midst of drafting necessary measures that look into increasing penalties for action against cable theft affecting public transport operators, including the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the proposed amendments would not be limited to ECRL, as cable theft was a problem affecting operators across the sector.
“Proposals to increase penalties for cable theft must go through parliamentary process.
“We are currently drafting the necessary measures,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Exhibition (TXA) here today.
He however said operators must also strengthen preventive measures, warning that tougher penalties alone would not resolve the problem if effective prevention was not in place.
“Whatever penalties are imposed, if preventive measures are not implemented effectively, they will not solve the problem,” he said.

The minister said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) and other operators were exploring additional ways to prevent cable theft, including the use of closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveillance and other technologies.
He added cable theft was not unique to Malaysia, but also affected transport operators in other parts of the world.
“I encourage companies and start-ups to develop innovative solutions to address the problem, including through research and development.
“This is how exhibitions such as TXA could provide a platform for companies to present solutions to operational challenges faced by transport operators,” he said.
Yesterday, the police busted four gangs suspected of cable theft belonging to ECRL and Telekom Malaysia (TM).
712c5174c2f1d7c1: TAIPEI: Workers at a Micron Technology plant in Taiwan plan to strike on Thursday as they aim to pressure the US chip firm into proposing a "concrete profit-sharing plan", a labour union representing the employees said.

Huge global appetite for chips used in AI data centres has sent revenues soaring for firms that design, produce and assemble them, but as their earnings skyrocket, workers are demanding a bigger cut of profits.
Monday's announcement came as Micron held talks over remuneration with two unions representing 12,000 of the 15,000 workers at its Taoyuan and Taichung plants.
The union representing hundreds of workers in Taoyuan said Thursday's strike would coincide with mediation talks with the company. It did not specify how long the strike could last.
"The strike aims to strengthen the union's position in mediation and urge Micron to put forward a concrete profit-sharing plan," the union said in a statement.
"We call on all Micron Taiwan Union members to stand together, fight together, and negotiate collectively," the union said.
"Through our actions, we will make our dissatisfaction with the current system heard and demonstrate our determination to establish a fair profit-sharing system."
Micron said it would issue a statement in response to the strike action later.
The workers have the legal right to strike and stage picket lines after voting earlier this month in favour of action, the union said previously.

The unions are seeking a one-off bonus of 83 months' salary as well as a permanent system that allocates 15% of the company's operating profits to worker bonuses, distributed quarterly rather than annually.
Micron, which makes around 50%-60% of its chips in Taiwan, said last month it would give the equivalent of up to 68 months of pay to staff, but the one-off payment was rejected by workers.
acaf0059beeac86e: PETALING JAYA: The husband of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer found murdered at a public housing complex in Nilai last week has a criminal record of 16 offences, police said today.
Nilai police chief Johari Yahya said 10 of the offences were drug-related while the remaining six involved burglary, theft and the possession of stolen property.
A preliminary urine screening test on the suspect, who is in his 30s, returned negative for drugs, he said.
Johari said police had recorded statements from 18 people to assist in the investigation.
"The investigation is ongoing, and we will refer the investigation papers to the prosecution on Wednesday for further action," he was quoted as saying by Sinar Harian.
He also said that police received no reports on any marital problems faced by the victim.
The 35-year-old woman was allegedly killed by her husband at about 7pm on Oct 15. He reportedly surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, after the incident.

The killing was believed to have stemmed from a marital dispute, with the victim reportedly having asked for a divorce. The suspect was recently released from prison after serving time for a drug offence.
A post-mortem examination found that the victim died from pressure on her neck. It also found stab wounds on the side of her abdomen and cheek.
4df360fa8f02a41d: Sony last week revived its famed Walkman brand of portable music players, with a trio of updated products that feature Android 16, touch screens, eye-popping prices, and dubious assertions of audiophile appeal.

The Japanese giant named the new models the NW-WM1ZM3, NW-WM1AM3 and NW-ZX900. All can store and play many codecs, including MP3s, WMA, and FLAC files, plus others like Direct Stream Digital (DSD) and Apple Lossless, which use various tricks to avoid nasty artefacts accruing during the digitization process.
Sony also says it has used “key components made from oxygen-free copper” because that apparently delivers “uncompromising sound quality.”

The machines also include “screws featuring a low-resistance gold-plated treatment … providing a stable ground connection that delivers powerful bass, an expansive soundstage and smooth, extended high frequencies.” Sony claims even the cabling it’s used in the devices “further reduces noise and preserves signal integrity for rich, detailed sound.”
They’re also housed in carefully-milled slabs of copper – gold-plated in the case of the NW-WM1ZM3 – because that apparently improves sound, too.
And then Sony’s gone and spoiled it all by offering Bluetooth connectivity, a notorious music-mangler, in addition to wired headphone ports.

Sony’s US site lists all three devices, which run Android 16 and include Wi-Fi so they can access streaming music services. All are USB-chargeable and Sony claims their batteries allow 30-odd hours of music playback.
The NW-ZX900 packs a five-inch touch screen and 64GB of onboard memory. It’s the baby of the range at just $1,900.
The NW-WM1AM3 will set you back $3,000, which buys 128GB of memory and a 5.5-inch screen.
The flagship NW-WM1ZM3 has the same size screen and includes 256GB of memory. It’s also a ‘Droid.
Don’t bother trying to put these under a Christmas tree because Sony says it will ship them mid-January. ®
1a7e0b08f7e67dda: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Pengarah Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan Malaysia (AKPS) Shuhaily Zain akan dituduh esok berhubung dakwaan mendatangkan kecederaan terhadap dua anggota polis di KLIA.
Peguam Negara Dusuki Mokhtar ketika mengesahkan perkara itu, berkata Shuhaily bakal berdepan dua pertuduhan mengikut Seksyen 323 Kanun Keseksaan kerana sengaja menyebabkan kecederaan.
"Beliau akan berdepan dua pertuduhan di Mahkamah Majistret Sepang," katanya ketika dihubungi.
Kes berkenaan tular selepas rakaman litar tertutup (CCTV) yang didakwa memaparkan Shuhaily bersemuka seorang individu di Terminal 1 KLIA.
AKPS mengesahkan rakaman CCTV tersebut adalah tulen, sambil menyatakan insiden itu berlaku semasa Shuhaily sedang memeriksa persiapan di KLIA menjelang Grand Prix Bahrain di Malaysia.
Shuhaily mendakwa pihak tertentu cuba mencemarkan reputasinya dan AKPS, namun beliau menegaskan akan memberi kerjasama penuh kepada siasatan dan menerima apa jua keputusan dibuat pihak berkuasa.
ab9d4b7cab4f6ad2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysian enforcement agencies have frozen up to RM4.3 billion in funds and 2.1 million shares up to 2026 as part of ongoing anti-money laundering operations, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament today, citing police enforcement statistics.
Anwar said his government has stepped up efforts to crack down on white-collar crime, which resulted in billions of ringgit seized and hundreds of prosecutions.

Between 2022 to September 2026, the Securities Commission has initiated 239 criminal charges against 50 individuals or entities compared to just 76 charges against 33 individuals or entities during the same period from 2017 to 2021.
“The total number of criminal charges has increased more than threefold,” Anwar, who is also finance minister, said during PM Question Time.

The network of corporate crime cases that have been rampant includes criminal acquisition and takeover of companies listed on Bursa Malaysia as well as private companies, stock market manipulation, violations of corporate disclosure and regulatory laws, and illegal money-lending activities, he added.

The government had seized an additional RM1 billion along with 2.1 million shares during the same period, while other enforcement actions further resulted in RM48 million in forfeited assets and RM1.1 billion in financial compounds issued to offenders.
“An additional sum of more than RM3 billion remains subject to ongoing court forfeiture proceedings aimed at recovering assets for the government,” Anwar said.
ecf56287ecd8d18d: TOKYO: Tokyo said Tuesday it was "extremely regrettable" that its diplomats had been unable to visit a Japanese journalist detained in Russia, despite a bilateral protocol that guarantees the right to consular access.
Russia arrested the journalist from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on the Far East island of Sakhalin a week ago on suspicion of espionage.
Moscow has arrested several citizens of what it calls "unfriendly" countries in recent years, accusing them of working for Western intelligence services.
Japan has denied the spying allegation and demanded that Russia release the man.

Chief cabinet secretary Minoru Kihara said the protocol, which was signed between Japan and the Soviet Union and remains effective with Russia, ensures the right to consular access within "a period of no later than four days from the time of arrest or detention".
"It is therefore extremely regrettable that, despite this provision, a consular visit was not realised within the prescribed period," Kihara said.

Japan will "continue to strongly urge the Russian side to arrange a consular visit at the earliest possible time", he said, adding that Tokyo was also demanding his release, humanitarian consideration, and fair treatment.
Russian media reported that the journalist would remain in custody until Dec 12.
Moscow's foreign ministry last week identified the arrested reporter as Yuki Imai, with a spokeswoman saying he was accused of "conducting espionage activities on Russian territory".
Russia's FSB security service said a Japanese national was arrested on Sakhalin - near a disputed cluster of islands - but did not name the individual.
It said the person had worked for Japanese intelligence to collect information about Russia's defences.
Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi denied the spying claim, saying "there is no such fact".
Tokyo summoned Russian ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev to lodge a protest over the arrest.
Moscow and Tokyo have been locked in a territorial dispute for decades over the status of a string of islands off the northeast coast of Japan and to the southwest of Russia's Sakhalin region.
The Kuril Islands - called the Northern Territories in Japan - have been under Russia's control since the end of World War II, when they were seized by the Soviet Union.
c7ca8824ae8b000b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has halted approvals for the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) to use the Selected Pre-Qualified Open Tender (TTPKT) method for new projects following findings in the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2025.

The ministry said the TTPKT method was introduced in 2023 as a special procedure to expedite the implementation of high-impact projects for the public and remained in place until June 30, 2025, with several enhancements aimed at strengthening government procurement governance.

“However, the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2025 found that that the implementation of the TTPKT method, including by the KKDW, had not achieved the government’s original objectives,” the ministry said in a written reply published on Parliament’s portal.

The ministry was responding to a question from Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) regarding action against KKDW officials responsible for authorising spending that exceeded allocations by RM2.1 billion between 2023 and 2025, as well as whether the contractors involved had been appointed through open tender.
According to the MOF, contractors for the Rural Road Programme under the KKDW are generally selected through tender processes, including open tender and the TTPKT method.

The ministry said the KKDW had, over the past few years, made financial commitments and incurred expenditure exceeding the original allocations approved in the annual budgets for rural road projects, resulting in arrears and delays in payments to contractors.
In this regard, the MOF said it had taken additional measures, including directing the KKDW to suspend the issuance of new Letters of Acceptance (SST) for rural road projects on September 10.

The ministry said it had also approved an additional RM500 million in expenditure for 2026 through a letter authorising expenditure beyond the approved allocation, after savings were identified in other ministries’ development expenditure.

In addition, the MOF said it had asked the KKDW to prepare projections of funding requirements for rural road projects up to the end of 2026 and for 2027, based on contracts already awarded, to determine the additional allocation needed.
According to the MOF, the original allocations approved for rural road projects under the annual budgets were RM1.09 billion in 2023, RM1.32 billion in 2024 and RM1.57 billion in 2025.

“To reduce payment arrears, the KKDW took steps to reallocate existing development expenditure funds from other projects through an internal Notice of Change (NOC) to meet the funding requirements of rural projects,” it said.

The MOF said the measure resulted in the allocations being revised to RM1.85 billion in 2023, RM2.02 billion in 2024 and RM2.27 billion in 2025, but the amounts were still insufficient to cover the ministry’s project commitments.
To address the issue, the MOF said it had agreed to increase the allocations for rural road projects to RM2.11 billion in 2026 and RM2.27 billion in 2027.
Meanwhile, the ministry said the adjusted allocation for 2026 stood at RM2.40 billion, with RM2 billion in expenditure recorded as at August 31. — Bernama
20457dc88e75c9bf: PETALING JAYA: Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Shuhaily Zain is expected to be charged tomorrow over the alleged assault of two police personnel at KLIA.
Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed the matter, saying Shuhaily would face two charges under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt.
"He will face the two charges at the Sepang magistrates' court," he said when contacted by the media.
The case came to public attention after CCTV footage allegedly showing Shuhaily confronting a person at KLIA Terminal 1 went viral.
AKPS confirmed the footage was genuine and said the incident occurred while Shuhaily was inspecting preparations at KLIA ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Shuhaily claimed that certain quarters were attempting to tarnish his reputation and that of AKPS, but said he would cooperate with the investigation and accept whatever decision the authorities make.
0f3a7794aa812e8b: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that no order has been issued to halt or postpone investigations into Zetrix AI Sdn Bhd and Felda, insisting that enforcement agencies are free to carry out their duties.
Anwar acknowledged that some investigations took a long time but said delays did not mean the government was protecting anyone from legal action.
"Are there instructions for the investigation to continue? Yes. Is there a closing order? No," he said during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat.

Anwar was responding to a supplementary question from Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) on the progress of investigations into several high-profile cases involving Zetrix AI, Tabung Haji (TH) and Felda.

Fadhli asked why investigations into Felda and TH, involving issues that allegedly occurred years ago, had only recently progressed, while the latest case involving Zetrix AI had not received similar attention.
In response, Anwar said the road transport department lodged a police report concerning Zetrix AI, while the Securities Commission Malaysia also launched investigations into the matter.
He said a white paper on Felda was tabled in 2019, but follow-up action only began after his government took power in 2022.
He said the government had established a special task force to examine the matter, and about a year had passed before investigation papers were opened.
"Felda's investigation papers were referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers several times for further scrutiny, which contributed to the lengthy process.
"I accept that there may sometimes be delays, but delays are better than taking no action at all," he said, adding that he had no intention of abusing his power to obstruct investigations.
On TH, he said the pilgrims' fund's issues were also brought to the Cabinet after his government took office.
He said TH's management requested that action be deferred while the institution pursued recovery efforts, but the investigation was still allowed to proceed.
b149b6a83cb60330: PETALING JAYA: The deregistration of Perikatan Nasional (PN) proves that Bersatu was in the right when it lodged its complaint over the coalition’s management on Aug 11, the party's secretary-general Azmin Ali said today.

He said the party explained to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) in August how the PN leadership had denied its rights guaranteed under the coalition’s constitution, in breach of the Societies Act 1966.
Azmin also took aim at PAS, saying it was portraying itself as a political victim in PN’s deregistration and attempting to garner sympathy ahead of the Melaka election.

"Stop the propaganda and extreme identity politics. The fact is that PAS failed to manage an organisation based on the principles of democracy and good management, and frequently betrayed its partners.
"PN cannot be a refuge for a group that is power-hungry and has sought to hijack the PN brand, which is moderate, progressive and responsive to the needs of Malaysians," he said in a statement.
Azmin said Bersatu would examine the RoS's decision in full and discuss the party’s next steps at a Supreme Council meeting.
Earlier today, the RoS said PN's Oct 12 response to a show-cause notice dated Sept 22 failed to justify retaining its registration.

It said the reasons given "could not rebut the grounds for deregistration, and did not provide strong justification for maintaining the society’s registration". However, it did not say what the grounds were or what PN had argued.
PN and PAS secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan questioned the timing of the deregistration, alleging that it raised concerns about political motives ahead of the Melaka state election.
Takiyuddin said the RoS issued its show-cause notice on Sept 22, the day the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly was announced, and suspended PN's activities the following day.
The deregistration, meanwhile, came just 11 days before nomination day for the state election.
06f90b75f9ead41f: LONDON, Oct 20 — James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham’s starting line-up on Monday as Roberto De Zerbi’s men beat Coventry 3-1 to claim their first Premier League win of the season.

On a feel-good night in London, Maddison marked his first start in 17 months with a spectacular early goal while Dejan Kulusevski returned to the matchday squad after missing the whole of last season.

Jack Rudoni levelled early in the second half but the home side were back in front just before the hour mark when Omar Marmoush lashed home his first goal for the club and substitute Ben Davies made the points safe in added time.

“I just wanted to play well, I just wanted to show my qualities and show what I bring to the team and what the team’s missed in the last 18 months or whatever it is from my last start,” Maddison told Sky Sports.
“So the gaffer asked me to play and he wanted to enjoy watching me from the side, so hopefully I did that.”
The Spurs playmaker said he believed he could help propel his team up the table as they seek to avoid the indignity of last season, when they narrowly escaped relegation.
“I’m 29, I’ve still got plenty of years left, and I have a lot of self-belief, and I know that I have quality that can really help us in this league,” he added.

Spurs came into the match rock bottom of the Premier League and with the unwanted record of being the only team in England’s top six divisions without a league win this season despite a huge summer outlay.
De Zerbi had taken his squad to Marbella in southern Spain for some warm-weather training in a bid to kickstart their season and it paid off against Frank Lampard’s competitive Coventry side.

Maddison, who ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee, put his side ahead in the 14th minute after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right.

Lurking just outside the penalty area, he received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans.
Maddison came close to doubling Spurs’ lead after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide.
Newly promoted Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range.
Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni’s effort hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him again and he drove home.
Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when Manchester City loanee Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing a powerful shot from distance.
Kulusevski, whose career was interrupted by a knee injury in May 2025, was brought off the substitutes’ bench in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans.
Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe in the dying minutes, poking home from the edge of the penalty area.
The win lifts Spurs up to 16th in the table, buying De Zerbi much-needed breathing space. — AFP
2bca3fec9410949f: TEHRAN: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tuesday that Russia and Iran have "never" worked so closely, as Moscow seeks to play a mediating role in the Middle East war.
Araghchi hosted his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov in Iran on Monday, in his first visit since the outbreak of the conflict.
"We covered everything from Europe to West Asia, including Lebanon, Palestine, Ukraine and Yemen. Also focused on expansion of economic and nuclear cooperation," Araghchi wrote on X.
"Never in our history have Iran and Russia worked as closely as now."
Lavrov said ahead of the visit that Moscow's efforts "aimed at preventing the return of a large-scale war", with talks stalled between the United States and Iran.
His visit came after Russian President Vladimir Putin told his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian this month that Moscow was prepared to contribute to mediation efforts.
Russia and Iran, two of the most heavily sanctioned nations in the world, maintain close ties.

The Middle East war erupted in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran. A ceasefire in April and a US-Iran memorandum of understanding in June have failed to stop fighting in and around the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran claims control over the strategic waterway – through which one-fifth of the world's oil passes in normal times – and regularly targets vessels that cross without its authorisation.
In response, Washington has been maintaining a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

The Russian foreign ministry said ahead of Lavrov's visit to Iran that discussions were expected to focus on "ways to resolve the acute international crisis triggered by the unlawful aggression of the US and Israel" against the Islamic republic.
The ministry said the war had been a blow to stability and security "not only in the near and Middle East, but also on a global scale".
1343a42cf1f7eb1b: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Kementerian Pembangunan Wanita, Keluarga dan Masyarakat (KPWKM) memperuntukkan kira-kira RM1 juta tahun ini bagi membantu wanita yang berdepan kesukaran kewangan, termasuk mangsa keganasan rumah tangga yang perlu membawa anak-anak dan meninggalkan pasangan mereka.

2a4fb4a32060d355: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government has yet to decide whether to raise the minimum age for obtaining a motorcycle licence.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the ministry is weighing the risk of pushing more underage riders onto the roads without valid licences.
“The proposal had been discussed years ago, but there were pros and cons to changing the current minimum age of 16.

“If you raise the age limit, secondary school students cannot get their licence. It will be a problem also, because then the student will ride motorcycles without a valid licence,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Exhibition (TXA) here today.
He noted that some students aged 13 or 14 were already riding motorcycles without licences despite the existing minimum age.
“This is not something which is a straightforward answer. It cannot just be about increasing the age limit,” he said.
The minister said the issue needed to be considered seriously, adding that at the moment there is yet to be a decision made on changing the minimum age for motorcycle licences.

He was responding to a proposal made by the Malaysian Road Safety Research Institute (Miros), that the minimum age for obtaining motorcycle licence should be raised to 18 to help curb illegal street racing for minors.
Miros chairman Professor Wong Shaw Voon cited this as a serious issue as it involved children as young as 12 who are riding without motorcycle licences.
